# Ringshadow

> Ringshadow: a free real-time strategy game for Mac, Windows and Linux. Your AI commander runs the army, and you can dive into any unit and play it like a shooter. Built in public with AI agents, public domain (CC0).

Source: https://ringshadow.com/

[Video: The camera dives from the top-down view into a Ranger, who walks out in first person](https://ringshadow.com/assets/media/dive.mp4) ![The command map: the bases of the map and the team's objectives](https://ringshadow.com/assets/media/command-map.jpg) ![The top-down view: the Citadel, its Stardust Ore line and two Metallic Hydrogen wells](https://ringshadow.com/assets/media/top.jpg)

## Play it three ways

### Drive any unit

Click one of your units and the camera dives in. `W``A``S``D` walks, the mouse aims, a click fires, `R` uses its ability, `V` switches first and third person, and `Esc` hands it back to the AI.

### Command the AI

Press `M` for the command map and give your team's AI its orders: a stance, objectives (attack, defend, hold, man a Bastion), expansions and requests. It plans the rest.

### Press the buttons

Click a building and press its buttons: train units, research, build. If it's a job the AI can do for you, the button queues it for your team's commander.

[Meet the twelve](#units)[How units level](#levels)

## Twelve you can drive

Nine on the ground, three in the air, each with its own cockpit, weapon and ability. These are frames from the game, as you see them when you dive in.

![A Prospector's drill at an ore deposit](https://ringshadow.com/assets/media/pilot-ore.jpg)

### Prospector

Worker

Mines ore, pumps MH, builds and repairs. Dull to drive, and the reason leveling exists.

![A Ranger firing its rifle](https://ringshadow.com/assets/media/pilot-ranger-fire.jpg)

### Ranger

Infantry

Rifle infantry. Its upgrades lean to firing and staying alive.

![A Comet in mid-jump](https://ringshadow.com/assets/media/pilot-comet-jump.jpg)

### Comet

Raider

A jump-pack raider with pistols that clears cliffs.

![A Juggernaut firing a grenade](https://ringshadow.com/assets/media/pilot-juggernaut-fire.jpg)

### Juggernaut

Grenadier

A heavy grenadier that breaks armour and slows what it hits.

![A Firefly firing its flame](https://ringshadow.com/assets/media/pilot-firefly-fire.jpg)

### Firefly

Buggy

A fast flame buggy. Its upgrades lean to burning and the flame's reach.

![A Longbow anchored as artillery](https://ringshadow.com/assets/media/pilot-longbow-anchored.jpg)

### Longbow

Tank

A tank that anchors into artillery. `R` anchors it.

![A Hailstorm firing flak](https://ringshadow.com/assets/media/pilot-hailstorm-fire.jpg)

### Hailstorm

Flak

A flak half-track that hits only flyers.

![An Atlas cockpit](https://ringshadow.com/assets/media/pilot-atlas.jpg)

### Atlas

Walker

A heavy assault walker. `R` fires its Quake stomp; its crew speaks with voices of its own.

![The Scorpion in its turnaround painting](https://ringshadow.com/assets/media/scorpion-painted.jpg)

### Scorpion

Mine

A burrowing mine. `R` buries it and digs it out again. No cockpit shot yet, so here it is from its turnaround painting.

![A Dropship healing the units below it](https://ringshadow.com/assets/media/pilot-dropship-heal.jpg)

### Dropship

Transport · air

A healing transport. `R` loads and unloads.

![A Kestrel firing rockets at the ground](https://ringshadow.com/assets/media/pilot-kestrel-fire.jpg)

### Kestrel

Gunship · air

A rocket gunship that strikes only the ground.

![A Peregrine's cockpit in flight](https://ringshadow.com/assets/media/pilot-peregrine.jpg)

### Peregrine

Fighter · air

An air-superiority fighter. `R` is the afterburner; its pilot has a voice of its own.

## Drive it and it levels

The longer you drive a kind of unit in a game, the better every unit of that kind gets. Units the AI runs never level, which gives you a reason to drive the dull ones.

![A level-up: two upgrade cards over the Prospector's cockpit](https://ringshadow.com/assets/media/level-cards.jpg)

- Drive: Only the units you drive yourself earn levels. Hand one back with `Esc` and it stops.
- Level: Each level lifts every unit of that kind on your side, for the rest of the game.
- Keep one: Every level offers two upgrades and you keep one: 216 across the twelve kinds, like "every Prospector pumps MH 20% faster".

## Life under the giant

[Video: A Prospector drilling Stardust Ore in first person](https://ringshadow.com/assets/media/mining.mp4)

*Ore and hydrogen Prospectors drill Stardust Ore and pump Metallic Hydrogen, and armies of up to eight players fight over the deposits.*

![The base at night, its beacons lit](https://ringshadow.com/assets/media/top-night.jpg)

*Night The sun crosses the sky; after dark the beacons and lamps come on.*

KSTR 88.7 Stardust The music plays as a radio station, with original songs.

Weather Sun, cloud, rain and storms on the game clock, wet ground and hulls after.

[Video: The camera pans across the base at dusk](https://ringshadow.com/assets/media/flyover.mp4)

*Dusk The camera pans over a base as the light goes.*

Ads between the songs Pumped from Metallic Hydrogen wells. "Not a beverage."

Face scrub Side effects: levitation, being mined.

Real estate Ash view guaranteed.

Everything above is the strategy game, playable today. Down here in the ring's shadow, the online world is being built.

## One pilot. A world that lasts.

![The giant's rings casting a dark band across the sky and land of the MMORPG world](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/how-we-got-here/06-ringshadow.webp)

### Playable now, as a test mode

Single player, on a local server that is the same program a public world will run. Your Prospector climbs to level 100 over about a hundred hours. A Citadel taxes, sells and hands out missions, mercenaries mine while the game is closed, and the Brood raids your buildings and eats your ore.

### Coming

Cities that pilots raise together with ore, MH and hours of labour. AI pilots with a city and a level of their own. And the no-man's land between the cities, where deposits and wells are taken and held by force.

[Read how it's being built](https://ringshadow.com/blog/)

## How it's made

### Concept to model

The model pipeline

![The Atlas six-view turnaround](https://ringshadow.com/assets/media/atlas-turnaround.jpg) Each unit starts as concept paintings. The one picked becomes a six-view turnaround, and the in-engine model is built part by part with Geometry Script and fitted against those views. The Atlas came to the game this way, and every snag along the road is written into the skill the agents follow.

[The model pipeline skill](https://github.com/ValiDraganescu/ringshadow/tree/main/.claude/skills/ringshadow-model-pipeline)

### An engine-free core

C++20, tests in 7 seconds

[Video: Two armies of twelve meet in the desert, seen from above](https://ringshadow.com/assets/media/fight.mp4) The whole simulation, from the economy and pathing to combat and the AI commanders, is plain C++20 with no Unreal in it. Its tests build with clang and run in about 7 seconds. The Unreal layer draws the frames, plays the sounds and takes the input.

[How the core is split](https://github.com/ValiDraganescu/ringshadow/blob/main/unreal/PORTING.md)

### Made by AI agents

The skills are in the repo

[Video: A Ranger walking in third person, recorded by the game's own recorder](https://ringshadow.com/assets/media/third.mp4) Ringshadow is made with AI coding agents, and the skills they work from are published with the code: the buildings' light language, which tests a change needs, and the recorder that makes every clip on this page from the real game.

[The skills](https://github.com/ValiDraganescu/ringshadow/tree/main/.claude/skills)

### Built in public

The blog and the roadmap

![A Prospector on its landing pad in the MMORPG mode, the ringed giant behind the clouds](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/how-we-got-here/cover.jpg) The blog follows the work as it lands, with the real numbers and the pictures from the day. The roadmap shows what is done and what comes next, and nothing past the done work has a date.

[The blog](https://ringshadow.com/blog/) [The roadmap](https://ringshadow.com/roadmap)

## Take any of it.

The game is free, and everything in the repository is public domain under CC0 1.0: the code, the art, the models, the sounds, the music and the docs. Use any of it for anything, with no credit needed.

All three builds and their checksums are on the [0.1.1 release page](https://github.com/ValiDraganescu/ringshadow/releases/tag/v0.1.1).

# The ring of Ringshadow

> The Ringshadow roadmap: what is done, what comes next and what comes later, from the strategy game to the MMORPG mode.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/roadmap

The roadmap

Every milestone is a moon on the giant's ring. What is done orbits in the sunlight. What comes next is turning into the shadow, and what comes later is still deep inside it. Scroll, and the ring turns.

- DONE: built, in the sunlight
- NEXT: the work in line, at the edge of the shadow
- LATER: planned, deep in the shadow

In the sunlight · done

## The strategy game

The real-time strategy game, playable today.

### A frontier RTS (Done)

Prospectors drill Stardust Ore and pump Metallic Hydrogen on Ashfall Reach, while armies of up to eight players clash over the deposits.

- An engine-free core: the economy, pathing, combat and the AI in plain C++20
- Its tests build with clang and run in about 7 seconds

### Twelve playable units (Done)

Prospector, Ranger, Comet, Juggernaut, Firefly, Dropship, Longbow, Kestrel, Hailstorm, Peregrine, Atlas and Scorpion, each with its own cockpit, weapon and ability.

- The last three joined the roster designed and built: an air-superiority fighter, a heavy assault walker, a burrowing mine
- The Peregrine pilot and the Atlas crew speak with voices of their own

### Dive into any unit (Done)

Click any of your units and the camera dives in. Drive it like a shooter, in first or third person, and hand it back to the AI with Esc.

- Shooter feel and night sight

### The AI commanders (Done)

Your team's AI commander runs the army. The command map gives it a stance, objectives, expansions and requests, and it plans the rest.

- Building buttons the AI can handle queue a request for it

### Pilot leveling (Done)

Drive a kind of unit and every unit of that kind gets better. Each level offers two upgrades and you keep one: 216 of them across the twelve kinds.

### Day, night and weather (Done · 2026-10-12)

The sun crosses the sky and the beacons come on at night. The weather runs on the game clock: clear, cloudy, rain and storms.

- Volumetric clouds, cloud shadows, wet ground and hulls, lightning and thunder

### KSTR 88.7 Stardust (Done)

The music plays as a radio station with original songs and in-world ads between them.

In the sunlight · done

## The engine and the name

### The Unreal port (Done · 2026-10-05)

The game began as a Swift and SceneKit live wallpaper. It now lives in Unreal Engine 5 only, and the Swift version is retired.

- Open source and public domain (CC0) from 2026-10-06

### It's called Ringshadow (Done · 2026-10-07)

The game was called Autocraft. It's named now for the huge ringed gas giant in its sky, the one the prospectors live in the shadow of.

- The GitHub repository took the name on 2026-10-09

### Three platforms, v0.1.0 (Done · 2026-10-09)

Release builds for Windows and Linux on a build machine in AWS, and the Mac build at home. The first pre-release, v0.1.0, is on GitHub.

In the sunlight · done · 2026-10-13

## The MMORPG mode, built so far

One pilot in a lasting world. Single player first, on a local server that is the same program a public world will run: only the host changes. Playable today as a test mode.

### Drive through a server (Done · M1)

The server is its own program, and the game is only its client. You drive a Prospector through it, over our own protocol on UDP.

- An authoritative server on the engine-free core
- Snapshots of only what is near you, sent as differences
- Prediction and correction, tested under made-up lag, jitter and loss

### The world map and regions (Done · M2)

A world of regions side by side, generated or crafted by AI agents with a region tool. Drive across an edge into the next region, or fly from pad to pad.

- The first world: three by three regions
- Build wherever it fits, paid from your wallet

### A world that lasts (Done · M3)

The server saves the world, and your pilot comes back as you left it: levels and picks included.

- A save every 5 seconds and on stop
- Resume your world, or start a new one

### Flights and polish (Done · M4)

Flights lift off, cross and land. The world map takes the keyboard, and the HUD is cut down to one pilot.

- Every screen checked picture by picture with a shot harness

### Ready to ship (Done · M5)

The traffic is encrypted, and the server travels inside the Mac package. The Metallic Hydrogen loop is proven: pump at a Derrick, unload at your Citadel, fill the wallet.

- X25519 and XChaCha20-Poly1305 through Monocypher (CC0)

In the sunlight · done · 2026-10-14

## A pilot's long road, under a living sky

A hundred hours of progression and a world with its own day, weather and events. The story is on the [blog](https://ringshadow.com/blog/how-we-got-here).

### A hundred levels and a living sky (Done · M6 · 2026-10-14)

The Prospector levels to 100, with a skill tree of 65 nodes in five branches. Buildings come from blueprints found in the world. The server owns the clock and the weather.

- Level 10 in about an hour, level 100 in about a hundred
- A 40-minute world day: 30 of light, 10 of night
- Foundry modules and Lab research

### A world worth crossing (Done · M7 · 2026-10-14)

The ringshadow sweep, starfall, KSTR contracts, blueprint sites you can see from afar, flights that burn MH, a guided first ten minutes and a new home screen.

- Starfall: two or three a world day, a crater with a rich deposit
- Three radio contracts a day

The terminator · next

## M8: the realm under siege

Buildings become the realm's, and the Prospector gets enemies. Nearly all of it has landed.

### The realm, the Brood and the defences (Next · M8)

Buildings belong to the realm, the Citadel taxes, sells and sends you on missions, and alien bugs swarm the places worth being. The realm has guns to hold them off, the Brood has its queen, and the first canyon plays as tower defence.

- Landed: the realm's buildings, the tax and the shop, missions and the Journal, the Brood, a world server that runs on after you quit, mercenary prospectors, the satellite map, the Citadel's turrets, the AA tower and the gatling gun, turret upgrades, the Matriarch at her nest, a ground for each region with walls and passages you walk through without a seam, the art pass on the Brood and the guns, a goal from the radio after the first ten minutes, a quieter HUD, regions shaped as valleys, the first canyon (The Fork), the Dropship between Landing Pads, the canyon's ten waves and the Matriarch's siege
- Still to come: a stability pass and a showreel

The terminator · next

## Next, in single player

Each step ships in the single-player game, on the local server.

### AI pilots (Next)

AI characters who are pilots themselves replace the AI commanders: a character, a city and a level, like a player. They mine, build, take contracts and fight, and keep the world busy where players are few.

### Cities (Next)

A city forms where pilots build close together. Its pilots raise it with ore, MH and hours of labour, and each level opens more. Cities are the safe places.

### More regions (Next)

A bigger world map, and travel between its regions.

### No-man's land (Next)

The open ground between the cities: claims, dwellings and the fight over the deposits and wells.

Deep in the shadow · later

## Later, online

The same server program, out in the world.

### The public server (Later)

The server on a public host, accounts and login, and other players in your world.

### The market, crews and chat (Later)

Trade between pilots, crews that ride together, and a way to talk.

### Thousands of pilots (Later)

Regions on separate servers, a pilot handed from one to the next at the border, and copies of the crowded places.

### Hosting (Later)

The official world on the Ringshadow AWS account, and a server build anyone can run for a world of their own.

Taken from the design docs and the work log in the [repository](https://github.com/ValiDraganescu/ringshadow). Nothing after the sunlit moons has a date yet.

# The packaged build, measured: a 1,547 ms stall down to 42

> Ringshadow's online mode packaged as a Mac app and measured, not shipped: it starts four times sooner than the editor, draws as fast, and the first Dropship call's 1.5-second stall is gone.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/blog/packaged

15 October 2026 · M9 · A living frontier

Everything on this blog so far ran inside the Unreal editor. Today an agent packaged the online mode as a Mac app and measured it the way the hidden runs measure the editor. Nothing is shipped: the app isn't published and this isn't a release. It's a measurement, and it found the real cause of a stall I'd felt from the first day.

![A bar chart on a log scale: the worst frame after a Dropship call 5 seconds into a session, packaged 1547 ms before and 42 after, editor 1628 before and 366 after, with startup times, canyon frame times and the app's size below](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/packaged/cover.jpg)

*The worst frame after calling the Dropship 5 seconds into a session, three runs each, before and after the fixes.*

## The stall

Call the Dropship in a session's first ten seconds and the game froze for over a second. It showed in the packaged app as much as in the editor, so the cause wasn't editor overhead, and it wasn't the call either: the session's first ten seconds were running at one to two seconds a frame, and a call landing there took one.

A trace named three causes. The game's own long jobs, a region made ahead, a ground set prepared, a minimap baked, about a second each, ran on the engine's thread pool, which is the two background workers the engine's task graph also uses. A 108 ms engine task the render thread was waiting on sat 860 ms behind them in the queue. Second, the baked console art read its copy back from the GPU as soon as it could, and on Metal a readback waits until the whole GPU is idle: 668 ms with the first frames queued. Third, the world map loaded each region's picture the first time it drew it, behind everything else the loader was reading, one to two seconds a picture.

The fixes: those jobs run on a thread pool of the game's own now, three threads; the art reads back once the GPU is calm; the map's pictures load as the world arrives. The worst frame after a call 5 seconds in went from 1,547, 92 and 32 ms over three packaged runs to 35, 37 and 42, and in the editor from 1,628, 78 and 160 to 366, 60 and 38. Frames over a quarter of a second in the first ten seconds: two or three a run before, none after, in the packaged app.

## What the package is like

It starts four times sooner than the editor: 3.0 to 4.2 seconds from the process starting to the first frame you drive, against 12.9 to 16.9. And it draws as fast as the editor's game. In The Fork with wave 10 out at noon, the median frame is 12.0 to 12.3 ms packaged and 12.5 to 12.6 in the editor at 1728 × 1084; at the nest in Slag Pockets with 34 bugs, 11.8 to 11.9 against 11.8 to 12.1. At 2560 × 1440 the canyon runs 13.0 to 13.4 ms packaged. Both the Development and the Shipping package take about three minutes to build; the Shipping app is 936 MB.

## What only the package showed

The weather wasn't cooked into the package, so a packaged game had no rain. The build script's cook check now fails on a gap like that. Two more ensures that the editor never hit, a rule naming a class the package lacks and run-time meshes without UV densities, are fixed too. The hidden-run tool learned to run a packaged app the way it runs the editor: offscreen, silent, no Dock icon, its own save and world server, one run at a time.

Every number here is from three hidden runs on the development Mac with other worktrees building beside them, and the full tables are in the repo's builds doc.

# Build anywhere in the canyon

> Ringshadow's canyons have no build spots any more: place any building anywhere standable in the zone, packed as tight as you like. The Brood walks round what it can and bites through what walls it off.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/blog/build-anywhere

15 October 2026 · M9 · A living frontier

I asked for this one: no more marked spots for the guns. You place any building anywhere you can stand in a canyon, on the rims, on the floor, across the Brood's path itself, packed as tight or as loose as you like. The walkers go round what they can and bite through what walls them off.

![Six Gatling Guns packed edge to edge beside The Fork's prize, their amber hoppers glowing](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/build-anywhere/cover.jpg)

*Six Gatling Guns edge to edge by The Fork's prize. A day ago this took six marked spots along the rim.*

My words to the manager: on the tower defence area I don't want explicit slots for what and where to build; players can place whatever anywhere, and pack the buildings as close or as far as they want. So the build spots are gone from all three canyons, and the ordinary rules are the only rules: the footprint has to fit on level, standable ground with nothing in the way, within your build reach, at the ordinary price and level floor, under the realm's limits. There's no spacing beyond the footprints, so guns pack side by side.

## Two cells to funnel, none to wall

The Brood's walkers now treat your buildings as the terrain they are. While any way to their next waypoint is open, they route round. When there is none, they bite through the nearest of your buildings, checking every half second. Gloamwings fly over as before. Buildings snap to whole cells and the walkers keep about a third of a cell off every footprint, so the narrowest gap they'll use is two cells. Pack tight to wall a way off, and they'll chew through; leave two cells, and they'll funnel through under your guns.

Measured at The Drowned Cut: with the Salt arm walled off, 3 of 4 walkers bit the line and none got past it; with a two-cell gap, 4 of 4 came through and the line was untouched.

## The straggler

The balance pass found a wave at The Fork that stayed out for over a thousand seconds, nineteen minutes, without reaching the guns or the prize. The cause was a hit Lodeback fleeing to the region's nearest edge, which was behind the canyon wall, and standing there until the wave's clock ran out. Now a leaving bug goes out by its own tunnel, and one that can get no nearer its exit for 4 seconds vanishes where it stands. A full cycle resolves every wave; the longest a wave stayed out was 16 seconds, and 12 Gatling Guns with 5 AA towers hold The Fork through wave 10, which they couldn't before.

## Small print

The turrets the Matriarch fells when a wave gets through are every gun within the zone's outline: 34 cells from the prize at The Fork, 43 at The Drowned Cut, 21 at The Roost. The [frontier pilots](https://ringshadow.com/blog/frontier-pilots) build no turrets in a canyon; their defender fights there and patrols the prize. All three canyons' region files, the map and the DEFENCE tab were redone for it, and the pictures of [The Fork's game](https://ringshadow.com/blog/canyon-game) and [the other two canyons](https://ringshadow.com/blog/two-canyons) were shot again on the new layout.

## In pictures

- ![Six Gatling Guns packed edge to edge beside The Fork's prize](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/build-anywhere/01-packed.webp) Packed: six guns with no gap between them.
- ![A Sentinel and a Gatling Gun on The Fork's rim, a tracer streaking from the gun](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/build-anywhere/02-rim-guns.webp) A Sentinel and a Gatling Gun on the rim, placed wherever they fit.
- ![A Gloamwing in the canyon hit by a burst from the Sentinels on the rim](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/build-anywhere/03-aa-fire.webp) A Gloamwing meeting the Sentinels' fire.
- ![The banner THE FORK HELD over the prize, KSTR: the canyon is the pilots' for a world day](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/build-anywhere/04-held.webp) THE FORK HELD, through wave 10 this time.
- ![The top-down preview of the Cold Fork region file: the zone's outline, the two tunnels, the Brood's paths and the prize, with no build spots marked](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/build-anywhere/05-cold-fork-preview.webp) The region file's preview after the change: the zone, the tunnels, the paths, the prize. No spots.

# The siege has a sound

> Two music beds for the canyon waves and the Matriarch, 28 radio lines from KSTR's announcer and the Dropship's engines, all made with ElevenLabs for Ringshadow.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/blog/siege-sound

15 October 2026 · M9 · A living frontier

Two music beds rise over the radio while a canyon is fought near you, one for the waves and one for the Matriarch, and KSTR's announcer now reads the canyon news and your next goal out loud. The Dropship got its engines too. All of it made with ElevenLabs, and all of it ours.

![The Dropship touching down on a Landing Pad at Prospect Landing in a cloud of dust, the wave panel reading THE FORK · HELD](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/siege-sound/cover.jpg)

*Touchdown at Prospect Landing after a held canyon: the flight sounds, then the radio comes back up.*

## The two beds

While a wave is out near you, or the game runs between waves, the wave layer plays over KSTR 88.7, the radio ducked under it. Its volume grows with the wave: 0.45 at wave 1, full at wave 10. When a wave breaks through and the Matriarch comes for the turrets, her layer takes over, and it plays whenever she stands in your region. Both fade in over 3 seconds and out over 4, and both go quiet the moment the canyon is held. The radio ducks to −24 dB in half a second and comes back over 2 seconds once they've gone.

The beds are ElevenLabs Music, instrumental, written for the game: a siege tension bed at 112 BPM in D minor for the waves, a boss dread bed at 84 BPM in C minor for her. An agent turned each into a seamless loop, half a second off the head, three seconds off the tail where the model writes its ending, and the last two seconds cross-faded over the start at equal power. They hold within 2 dB from end to end. Listen:

### The wave layer · 60.5 s loop

[Audio](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/siege-sound/siege-wave.m4a)

### The Matriarch layer · 44.5 s loop

[Audio](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/siege-sound/siege-matriarch.m4a)

## KSTR speaks

The station's announcer, the same glossy voice that reads the ads, now has 28 lines: one for each goal in the radio's chain and one for a goal done, and for each canyon a line for a wave incoming, a wave beaten, the canyon held and the canyon fallen. All of them are under six seconds. They go through a queue, one at a time with 0.6 seconds between, never over a mission narration, at most four waiting, and a line older than 20 seconds is dropped unread.

### The Fork has fallen

[Audio](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/siege-sound/kstr-fork-fallen.m4a) "The Fork has fallen! The Matriarch is coming for the turrets!"

### The Fork is held

[Audio](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/siege-sound/kstr-fork-held.m4a) "The Fork is held! A whole day of peace out there."

The Dropship's flight got its sounds from the same shop: the engines spooling on the pad, the roar of the lift-off, a cruise loop, the retro burst on the approach and the touchdown. They're ElevenLabs sound effects, and silent in the hidden test runs.

## Made offline, checked offline

Halfway through, ElevenLabs ran out of credits with 4 left and 5 of the 28 lines made, so the agent cut stand-in loops from two of our own retired tracks and kept going. I topped the account up the same day and everything was made for real: about 1,900 characters of speech and two music generations, 66 and 50 seconds. No run ever plays any of it aloud. Every cue is written to the game's log, the layers' levels, the radio's duck, each line, each flight sound, and a silent test run checks the timeline: a wave at The Fork brings its layer up and the radio down, a wave beaten reads its line, a breakthrough brings her layer and "has fallen", a hold takes both out and the radio back to full, a goal reached reads the next one, and a flight plays lift, cruise, retro and touch in order.

## Also landed: the map says why

Before, a Landing Pad you couldn't fly to just wouldn't pick. Now the map says why: only one pad in the realm, and where to build the second; that's the region's own pad and the Dropship lands only on a Landing Pad; or, when it can be picked, the fare.

## In pictures

- ![The Dropship down on a Landing Pad at Prospect Landing, dust settling, THE FORK · HELD on the panel](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/siege-sound/01-landed.webp) The flight's last cue, the touchdown, with The Fork held.
- ![The world map with a message: only one Landing Pad in the realm, here; walk to another region and build one to fly between them](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/siege-sound/02-map-only-here.webp) One pad in the realm: the map tells you to build the second.
- ![The world map with a message: that is the region's own pad; the Dropship lands only on a Landing Pad](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/siege-sound/03-map-own-pad.webp) A region's own pad can't be picked, and the map says so.
- ![The world map with a pad picked: FLY the Dropship to Landing Pad 1 in Rust Hollow for 15 MH](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/siege-sound/04-map-picked.webp) Picked: the Dropship to Rust Hollow for 15 MH.

# The balance pass: about ×2 the mining curve, never over ×2.5

> Ringshadow's balance pass: mission and canyon pay cut so that a pilot who mines, takes the board and holds a canyon runs about twice the mining curve, never over two and a half times.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/blog/balance

15 October 2026 · M9 · A living frontier

Missions and canyon waves paid far too well: a pilot who did everything levelled about four times as fast as one who only mined. The agents measured every number in the economy against the pace model, cut two of them, and left the rest alone.

![A bar chart of an hour of play in XP at levels 1, 5, 10, 15 and 20: the pace curve against the measured all-in pilot, ×1.86 to ×2.02, with the mission and wave pay before and after](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/balance/cover.jpg)

*An hour of play in XP, measured, against the curve the game is paced on.*

The rule the manager set: risk and play should pay better than mining, without collapsing the curve. A pilot who mines, takes the Citadel's board and holds a canyon runs about twice the mining curve, and never over two and a half times.

## How it was measured

A bench runs isolated scenes, never a whole game. A driven Prospector mines for ten game minutes at levels 1, 5, 10, 15 and 20 with three skill builds. The Fork's waves run for a level-15 pilot with its own guns on the rims. Then an hour of play is filled the way the pace model fills it: three quarters work, nine missions an hour from the board, from level 10 one canyon cycle every 70 minutes, and mining for the rest. A test suite pins every curve, so a later change breaks a test before it breaks the game.

## What changed

- Missions: pay 3, 8 and 15 minutes of play in XP for easy, hard and perilous, about three times the time they take. They paid 8, 20 and 40, eight to sixteen times the time. Their ore is halved: 75, 225 and 500.
- Canyon waves: pay 0.4 of before: 80 × n XP, 60 × n ore and 16 × n MH for wave n. Wave 10 still pays double, and a level-3 canyon still pays ×1.3.

With those two, the all-in pilot runs ×1.87, ×1.86, ×2.02, ×1.95 and ×1.89 the curve at levels 1, 5, 10, 15 and 20, and reaches level 10 in 36 minutes. Before, it was about ×4 and 18 minutes. Pure mining takes 66.

## What held

Mining itself: 7,884 ore an hour at level 1, of which the Citadel's 10% tax takes 936. Shop prices: a first blueprint costs a few minutes of income at its floor, from 1.2 minutes for a Citadel to 12.9 for a Bastion. Mercenaries earn at most an eighth of the pilot. A frontier pilot's booked mining is a quarter of a pilot's, so five of them give the realm at most 745 ore an hour. The turret marks pay for themselves within a cycle or two of a held canyon.

## Seen on the way

Twelve gatling guns and five AA towers alone don't hold The Fork: waves 9 and 10 break through, and in each run one straggler stayed out for over a thousand seconds without reaching the guns or the prize. That goes into the canyon work. And the realm wallet has only one thing to spend on, the Citadel's twelve marks, which one pilot's tax buys in six or seven hours. What the realm spends on after that is a design question for later.

The earlier posts on [missions](https://ringshadow.com/blog/missions) and [the canyon game](https://ringshadow.com/blog/canyon-game) carry the old figures with a note pointing here.


---

# Two more canyons: the brine and the roost

> Two more canyons in Ringshadow's world: The Drowned Cut in Brine Pans, a flooded basin where the Brood's walkers wade at half speed, and The Roost in Dust Terraces, a spire every Gloamwing launches from.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/blog/two-canyons

15 October 2026 · M9 · A living frontier

The Fork has company. The Drowned Cut in Brine Pans is a flooded basin where the Brood's walkers wade at half speed, and The Roost in Dust Terraces has a spire every Gloamwing launches from, over the walls and past the tunnels' guns.

![The Drowned Cut from above: a white salt mesa cut by two arms that meet at a flooded basin with the prize in its middle, yellow build spots on the rims, a wrecked hauler on the east shore](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/two-canyons/cover.jpg)

*The Drowned Cut from above: the Salt arm from the west, the Gull arm from the north, the brine in the basin.*

Each canyon plays [The Fork's game](https://ringshadow.com/blog/canyon-game): ten waves along its arms to a prize, the first replaying until beaten, the Matriarch if a wave gets through, the canyon held for a world day after the tenth. What each one adds is a twist of its own.

## The Drowned Cut, Brine Pans

Brine Pans is the salt flats, so its canyon is flooded. Two arms meet in a basin: the long Salt arm winding in from a tunnel in the west wall, and the short Gull arm dropping in from the north. The prize is five deposits of 6,000 ore round a 6,000 MH well, and a half-drowned hauler lies on the east shore. Seven build spots sit on the Salt arm's south rim, the basin's west rim and the north rim.

The brine covers the basin and the lower Salt arm, and the Brood's walkers wade through it at half speed, so they spend longer under the rims' guns. Gloamwings fly over it unslowed, and so do pilots: your Prospector's movement is predicted on your machine, and a slow the server applied alone would rubber-band you. The waves are walker-heavy for it, 120 walkers over the ten waves against The Fork's 115, with the mini-boss Lodebacks from wave 5.

Measured: the Salt arm takes 12.8 seconds to march through the brine against 10.7 dry. Of 2,104 samples of wading walkers, 2,104 were slowed; of 4,150 samples of flyers, none.

## The Roost, Dust Terraces

Dust Terraces is stepped sandstone with high ledges, which is where the Gloamwings roost. Its canyon is a mesa over the south-west terrace with two tunnels, the Ochre and the Dust, winding to a basin, and a spire rising at the basin's west edge with a nest of chitin on top. The prize is five deposits of 7,500 ore round a 7,500 MH well, with seven build spots on the rims.

The spire is the twist. One of the zone's entrances is a roost, a ledge and not a tunnel, and every Gloamwing of a wave comes off it, a level or more over the prize, and flies down over the walls. The walkers still come out of the tunnels. So the flyers come from the one place the tunnels' guns don't cover, and the AA towers belong by the spire. The warnings say it as it is: "14 bugs from the Dust tunnel and The Roost". It's a level-3 region, so the waves are heavier, 63 flyers over the ten against The Fork's 34, and wave 10 is 42 bugs.

The pay of a level-3 canyon is higher than The Fork's. The balance pass is going over every number in the economy right now, so the figures wait for it.

## In pictures

- ![The Drowned Cut from above: the salt mesa, two arms, the flooded basin and the prize](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/two-canyons/01-drowned-cut.webp) The Drowned Cut from above.
- ![A Lodeback wading through the salt-green brine at the mouth of the Salt tunnel](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/two-canyons/02-waders.webp) A Lodeback wading at half speed.
- ![The wave panel THE DROWNED CUT · WAVE 6 / 10, 16 bugs from the Salt and Gull tunnels](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/two-canyons/03-drowned-cut-wave.webp) Wave 6 of The Drowned Cut: 16 bugs from the Salt and Gull tunnels.
- ![The Roost from above: a sandstone mesa, two winding arms, the basin with the prize and the chitin nest on the spire](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/two-canyons/04-roost.webp) The Roost from above, the nest on its spire at the basin's west edge.
- ![Gloamwings launching off the spire's nest under a gatling gun's fire](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/two-canyons/05-gloamwings.webp) Gloamwings off the roost, under fire.
- ![The warning THE ROOST: WAVE 4 OF 10, 14 bugs from the Dust tunnel and The Roost, with the region banner DUST TERRACES](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/two-canyons/06-roost-wave.webp) Wave 4 of The Roost: 14 bugs from the Dust tunnel and The Roost.
- ![The world map on Brine Pans with the canyon's ring over the mesa](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/two-canyons/07-map-brine.webp) Brine Pans on the map, the canyon ringed.
- ![The world map on Dust Terraces with the canyon's ring in the south-west](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/two-canyons/08-map-dust.webp) Dust Terraces on the map.

## The same for every canyon

The states, the fail mark, the Matriarch's siege and the hold are The Fork's. A [frontier defender](https://ringshadow.com/blog/frontier-pilots) goes to any canyon whose wave a human is holding. And the save keeps each zone's row, so the three canyons' games carry on between sessions.

# By day you see the whole region

> By day a Ringshadow pilot sees its whole region, with every unit, bug and building sent; dusk eases the sight down to the night's. Measured at the nest and at The Fork.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/blog/daylight

15 October 2026 · M8 · The realm under siege

The regions aren't that big, so by day there's no fog: every unit, bug and building in yours is sent to you and drawn. Through dusk the sight closes in to the night's, round your headlamp, and opens again at dawn. This closes milestone 8.

![The Matriarch's nest in Slag Pockets at noon seen from far across the lava flats, the whole horde drawn, the HUD counting 27 enemies](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/daylight/cover.jpg)

*Slag Pockets at noon from 55 cells away: the nest, the Matriarch and her horde, all told to the client.*

My remark was short: by day the line of sight should be the whole region, since the zones are small. Until now a pilot saw what the fog of war allowed, by night and by day alike, and the server sent only that. That kept a hacked client from revealing anything, and it stays that way: nothing hidden by the fog ever leaves the server. What changed is what the fog allows by day.

## Day, dusk, night

By day a pilot sees all of its region, every level of it, so every unit, bug and building in it is sent, the far ones in fewer snapshots than the near ones. Through dusk the sight closes in round the driven unit to the night's: half its day reach plus the headlamp's wedge, easing down by the same share at each step of the lamps' dark, over about one game hour, which is about 100 real seconds. Night is unchanged. Neighbouring regions are as before.

Measured in Prospect Landing at dusk, the half-cells a pilot sees: 55,296 at 18.0 h, 22,256 at 18.3, 5,356 at 18.5 and 618 at 19.0.

One rule followed from it. A bug that has eaten its fill and is leaving used to vanish once it was out of the pilot's interest. Now it vanishes only out of real sight or at the region's edge, so by day you watch a Lodeback carry your ore all the way home.

## What it costs

The worry was bytes and frame time, so both were measured, at the two busiest places in the world.

| Scene at noon | Units told before | Now | Bytes a second to the client |
|---|---|---|---|
| The nest in Slag Pockets | 2 of 29 | 29 of 29 | 2,022 → 3,730 |
| The Fork, wave 10 out | 1 of 35 | 35 of 35 | 2,090 → 4,103 |

The server's world tick stays at 0.25 ms at the 99th percentile. In the game the frame is 12.2 to 12.7 ms median with or without the daylight sight, and the GPU 11.7 to 12.2 ms, so the extra units drawn cost nothing you'd notice.

## In pictures

- ![The nest in Slag Pockets at noon, the horde drawn from far away, 27 enemies on the HUD](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/daylight/01-nest-noon.webp) Noon, before and after: the whole horde at the nest, 27 enemies counted.
- ![The same view before: the nest in the distance with almost nothing drawn, 1 enemy on the HUD](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/daylight/02-nest-before.webp) Before: the same spot, one enemy told.
- ![The same view at night: only the lava-lit ground near the Prospector](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/daylight/03-nest-night.webp) Night is unchanged: the headlamp and the lava.
- ![The Fork at noon with wave 10 out, 34 bugs on the panel, the whole canyon drawn](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/daylight/04-fork-noon.webp) The Fork at noon with wave 10 out: all 34 bugs told.
- ![The Fork before: the wave panel counts 34 bugs but the canyon is empty](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/daylight/05-fork-before.webp) Before: the panel counts 34, the eye sees one.

The pictures also fixed a testing annoyance: the Brood and Matriarch shot sets had been failing their checks because the night's six-cell sight hid the scenes they were checking. They hold noon now.

Every test suite passes: 496 core, 279 server and 91 network.


---

# Frontier pilots: you're no longer the only one out here

> Five pilots of the server's own in every Ringshadow world: callsigns, paints and habits, mining, building, fighting and talking on the radio by the same rules as you.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/blog/frontier-pilots

15 October 2026 · M9 · A living frontier

A world with one pilot in it reads as empty. Now the server runs five pilots of its own in every world, each with a callsign, a paint and a habit, and they mine, build, take missions, fight bugs and talk on the radio by the same rules you play by.

![A frontier pilot's Prospector drilling an ore rock, the tag LARKSPUR · LV 34 over it](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/frontier-pilots/cover.jpg)

*Larkspur, level 34, a miner, drilling at Prospect Landing.*

This is the first piece of milestone 9, which the manager named a living frontier. The question behind it is what makes an evening worth logging in for, and the first answer is company.

## Who they are

Five per world by default, up to six. Their callsigns come from a list of twelve: Vesper, Kestrel, Corvid, Tamsin, Brindle, Sorrel, Moraine, Talus, Lumen, Calder, Drover and Larkspur, in the order the world's dice give. They wear the team paints, green, gold, violet, teal and pink, and never your blue or the mercenaries' orange. Each has a habit:

- Miners: drill and haul, put a Derrick on the well by their field, and raise a Hab Dome where the haul home is long.
- Builders: put up realm buildings where they help: a gatling gun by a field the Brood keeps raiding, a Landing Pad in a region that has a Citadel or a canyon and no pad. Otherwise they drill to earn their keep.
- The defender: joins a canyon wave whenever you are in that canyon's region, fights bugs near the realm's buildings, mends anything below 90% and patrols from building to building.
- The wanderer: opens the sites nobody has opened, takes surveys of the regions next door, and moves on, on foot or by Dropship when both regions have a pad.

## The same rules as you

No cheats. A frontier pilot starts with a new pilot's wallet, 600 ore and 40 MH, earns XP at the world's rates and levels on the same curve, spending its points down its habit's branch of the skill tree. It buys blueprints at the Citadel at the shop's price, builds at the blueprint's floor and under the realm's limits, pays the tax on every unload and the fare for every flight. Its buildings belong to the realm, like yours. What it can't have is your skills' boosts: the core gives those only to the unit you drive.

Caps keep the realm yours: at most eight of their buildings in a world, one Hab Dome, two Derricks, two gatling guns, one Landing Pad per region, and never the last slot under a limit. That one is always left for a human. They never build a Citadel, a Foundry, a Lab, a Spacedock, a Bastion or an AA tower.

## When they come

They arrive once a human has finished the opening chain, by Dropship, 45 seconds later, one every 40 seconds, each announced to everyone with a hello on the radio. While you are still on the chain, they keep 14 cells off its places: the start pad, its two sites, the nearest deposit and the well.

Where you can see them, their Prospectors are real units in the simulation, steered with the core's own orders. Everywhere else their work is booked on the world's clock, a straight-line walk and a drill's worth of ore per trip, so a miner in a region nobody is looking at still fills its wallet. Unlike the mercenaries, they don't catch up time the server was down.

## In pictures

- ![Larkspur's Prospector drilling an ore rock at Prospect Landing, its tag over it](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/frontier-pilots/01-miner.webp) Larkspur, a miner, at work beside the human.
- ![A freshly built Hab Dome and the toast ON THE FRONTIER: Sorrel built a Hab Dome in Prospect Landing](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/frontier-pilots/02-builder.webp) A deed on the frontier: Sorrel built a Hab Dome.
- ![The toast KSTR · SORREL: Bugs inbound at Prospect Landing. Sorrel sees them, keep your heads down](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/frontier-pilots/03-radio.webp) Sorrel on the radio when the Brood's raid is called.
- ![The world map with the frontier pilots' dots in their paints](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/frontier-pilots/04-map.webp) Their dots on the map, in their paints.
- ![The map tooltip LARKSPUR · LV 34, Frontier pilot · Miner, Mining in Prospect Landing](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/frontier-pilots/05-tooltip.webp) Hover one: who, what, where.
- ![Brindle's Prospector at The Fork's prize among the ore rocks](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/frontier-pilots/06-defender.webp) Brindle, the defender, at The Fork.
- ![The defender at The Fork with the wave panel up](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/frontier-pilots/07-defender-hud.webp) Fighting the wave beside you, paid by damage like anyone.
- ![A frontier pilot at night, its tag in the headlamp's light](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/frontier-pilots/08-night-tag.webp) At night a tag shows only over a unit you can actually see.

## What you see

Their Prospectors wear a tag, "VESPER · LV 14", and the first pictures showed tags floating with nothing under them, over units the fog or the distance hid. A fix the same morning draws a tag only over a unit you can see: drawn, inside the sight's light, with no ground or building between the camera and its head. The mercenaries' tags follow the same rule.

On the map each one is a dot in its paint, with a tooltip for its name, habit and what it is doing. Notable deeds come as toasts headed ON THE FRONTIER: "Tamsin opened the Ridge wreck in Cold Fork", "Kestrel built a Derrick in Prospect Landing". And they talk on KSTR: a hello on landing, a warning when a raid is called, a cheer when a wave is beaten ("Wave down at The Fork. Brindle owes somebody a drink"), a cry for help when one is badly hurt, and chatter at most every ten world minutes.

Every test suite passes: 496 core, 279 server and 91 network.


---

# The realm under siege: the M8 showreel

> The M8 showreel: 67 seconds of the Brood, the Citadel's guns, the Dropship, The Fork and the Matriarch, cut the morning after I asked the agents for all of it.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/blog/realm-under-siege

15 October 2026 · M8 · The showreel

On the evening of 14 October I played the online mode up to level 10 and asked "now what?". By 08:14 the next morning the agents had built the answer and cut a reel of it: 67 seconds of the Brood, the Citadel's guns, the Dropship, The Fork and the Matriarch, to one of our own songs.

[Video: The M8 showreel: a passage into the next valley, the Citadel's screens, the Brood at the ore, the corner guns, the Dropship's flight, the satellite map, a wave down The Fork, the Matriarch felling the turrets and her nest](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/realm-under-siege/showreel.mp4)

*The M8 showreel, 67 seconds, recorded from the game by an agent in hidden runs. The music is Rising Pressure, one of our own songs.*

Every beat of the reel has its own post on this blog, so this one is the tour. The times are where each beat starts.

## 0:00 · Dawn, and a valley without seams

Prospect Landing at dawn under the ringed giant, then out through a passage into the next valley. Region borders follow the land now, 14 passages join the 9 regions, and crossing on foot hands you from one region to the next without a seam. [The passages](https://ringshadow.com/blog/passages) and [the valleys](https://ringshadow.com/blog/valleys).

## 0:08 · The Citadel

The realm screen, the shop, the missions board and the Journal. The Citadel takes 10% of every unload into a realm wallet, sells four consumables and every blueprint, and offers missions in three tiers, each with a narration. The reel's one spoken line is the Warden's: "When the ring's shadow crosses the land, the ground goes cold and the dark comes alive." [The realm](https://ringshadow.com/blog/the-realm) and [the missions](https://ringshadow.com/blog/missions).

## 0:17 · The Brood

Shardlings at the ore, a Gloamwing diving, a Lodeback hauling ore off in its sac. Four kinds of bug, drawn to the places worth being, and with 17 to 19 of them on screen the mean frame time went from 10.42 ms to 10.77 ms. [The Brood](https://ringshadow.com/blog/the-brood) and [their art pass](https://ringshadow.com/blog/brood-art).

## 0:24 · The raid

KSTR calls a swarm heading for the Citadel, and its four corner guns answer. Then the gatling gun's red-hot amalgam rounds. [The defences](https://ringshadow.com/blog/defences) and [the turret upgrades](https://ringshadow.com/blog/turrets).

## 0:28 · The Dropship

Board at a Landing Pad, a banked turn past the giant, down on the pad in a new region, 16 to 20 seconds without a fade. [The Dropship](https://ringshadow.com/blog/dropship).

## 0:36 · The map

The world map is a satellite view of the real ground of every region you've seen, with tooltips on everything in it. [The world map](https://ringshadow.com/blog/world-map).

## 0:42 · The Fork

A wave down the canyon's arm, guns on the rim. Ten waves, 34 bugs in the last, and a wave breaks through when it carries off 300 ore of the prize. [The Fork](https://ringshadow.com/blog/the-fork) and [holding it](https://ringshadow.com/blog/canyon-game).

## 0:52 · The Matriarch

She comes out of the tunnel the wave came from, fells every turret in the canyon nearest first, and goes home to her nest in Slag Pockets, which is where the reel ends. [The Matriarch](https://ringshadow.com/blog/matriarch).

## How the reel was made

An agent recorded each beat with a shot script that drives the game through hidden runs: the game runs invisible and silent, one run at a time on the whole Mac, and a clip mode drops the HUD for the clean moments. A cut file lists each shot's source, in and out points, zoom, focus, kicker and caption; a script pans, subtitles and joins them with half-second crossfades, and puts the end card over the key art. The music is Rising Pressure, one of our Suno songs, mixed at −16 LUFS. Between the first task of the milestone and the reel, 137 commits landed on the integration branch.

Before the reel, a stability pass fixed the flaky checks at their causes and reran everything on the current build: 27 shot sets, 6 flows, 92 of 92 automation tests, and the suites at 496 core, 267 server and 88 network tests, all passing.

The next milestone is a living frontier. Its first piece landed the morning after the reel: five pilots of the server's own in every world, with callsigns, paints and habits, playing by the same rules as you. That post is next.


---

# Holding The Fork: ten waves, and the Matriarch if you fail

> The canyon game is in Ringshadow: ten waves of the Brood down The Fork's two arms, guns on the rims, and if a wave breaks through, the Matriarch comes out of the tunnel and fells every turret.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/blog/canyon-game

15 October 2026 · M8 · The realm under siege

This was my idea for the canyons: tower defence inside the world. [The Fork](https://ringshadow.com/blog/the-fork) was cut earlier today; now it plays. The Brood comes down its arms in waves, the pilots hold the rims with [their guns](https://ringshadow.com/blog/turrets), and if a wave gets through, the queen comes to tear the guns down.

![The Matriarch rearing out of a tunnel in the canyon wall, her crown spread, between turrets on the rims](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/canyon-game/cover.jpg)

*A wave broke through: the Matriarch comes out of its tunnel, between the rim turrets.*

## The opening wave

While a pilot is in Cold Fork or next to it, the opening wave comes every 3 minutes: four Shardlings down one arm, taking the other arm the next time. It repeats until the pilots beat it, with turrets or with their own torches, and losing it costs nothing. Beating it starts the game.

## Ten waves

Waves 2 to 10 come one at a time, with a 30-second countdown between them. From wave 3 they use both arms. Gloamwings arrive at wave 4, which is what the AA towers are for. Waves 5 and 10 are the mini-bosses: hoards of Lodebacks, heavily escorted, going straight for the ore. Wave 10 is 34 bugs.

| Wave | North arm | East arm | Bugs |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4 Shardlings, one arm, turning each time | 4 |
| 2 | 6 Shardlings |  | 6 |
| 3 | 5 Shardlings | 5 Shardlings | 10 |
| 4 |  | 7 Shardlings, 3 Gloamwings | 10 |
| 5 | 2 Lodebacks, 6 Shardlings | 4 Gloamwings | 12 |
| 6 | 8 Shardlings, 4 Gloamwings | 4 Shardlings | 16 |
| 7 | 7 Shardlings | 7 Shardlings, 1 Lodeback, 3 Shardlings | 18 |
| 8 | 5 Gloamwings | 5 Gloamwings, 8 Shardlings | 18 |
| 9 | 10 Shardlings | 2 Lodebacks, 4 Shardlings, 5 Gloamwings | 21 |
| 10 | 3 Lodebacks, 10 Shardlings, 4 Gloamwings | 3 Lodebacks, 10 Shardlings, 4 Gloamwings | 34 |

A wave is beaten when every bug in it is dead. It breaks through if its bugs carry off 300 ore of the prize, counting what Shardlings gnaw and what Lodebacks haul away in their sacs, or if its time runs out with bugs still on the prize. A Lodeback killed before it gets away gives its ore back.

A panel under the compass shows the wave, the bugs left and the ore taken against the 300 mark. KSTR warns which tunnels a wave is coming from, the map rings the canyon, and the Journal has a line for it. The waves pause when no pilot is near, so the world can run on while you're away without losing turrets to a fight nobody saw.

## A game in The Fork

- ![Four Shardlings coming down the north arm past a Sentinel on the rim](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/canyon-game/01-wave-1.webp) The opening wave, down the north arm.
- ![The wave panel under the compass: THE FORK, wave 1, the opening wave, 4 bugs left, ore taken out of 300](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/canyon-game/02-panel.webp) The wave panel: bugs left, ore taken out of 300.
- ![A Sentinel and a gatling gun firing from the rim](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/canyon-game/03-rim-guns.webp) The rim guns firing.
- ![THE FORK: WAVE 1 BEATEN and YOUR SHARE toasts, the panel counting down to wave 2](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/canyon-game/04-beaten.webp) Wave 1 beaten, the share paid, wave 2 counting down.
- ![The banner THE FORK HAS FALLEN: wave 4 broke through, the Matriarch comes for its turrets](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/canyon-game/05-fallen.webp) Wave 4 broke through: THE FORK HAS FALLEN.
- ![The Matriarch rearing out of the tunnel between turrets](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/canyon-game/06-matriarch.webp) She comes out of the wave's tunnel.
- ![The Matriarch's slam blowing a turret apart on the rim](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/canyon-game/07-fells.webp) And fells the turrets, nearest first.
- ![The prize full again, the panel back at wave 1, the opening wave](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/canyon-game/08-reset.webp) The reset: wave 1 again, the prize full.
- ![The banner THE FORK HELD: the canyon is the pilots' for a world day](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/canyon-game/09-held.webp) THE FORK HELD: no waves for a world day.
- ![The world map of Cold Fork with a ring round The Fork](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/canyon-game/10-map.webp) The canyon ringed on the map.

## When a wave gets through

The whole world hears THE FORK HAS FALLEN. [The Matriarch](https://ringshadow.com/blog/matriarch) comes out of the tunnel that wave came from, with six Shardlings, fells every turret in the canyon, nearest first, and goes home. A felled turret loses its marks. The zone resets to the opening wave with the prize refilled, and the next wave waits 3 minutes so the pilots can rebuild. If someone kills her out there, the turrets she hasn't reached yet stand. If she's already dead and not yet back, she can't come: the zone resets and every turret stays.

## When the pilots hold

Beat wave 10 and the whole world hears THE FORK HELD. For a world day, 40 minutes, no waves come and the prize is the pilots' to mine. Then the opening wave starts again.

Every wave beaten pays everyone who fought it, split by the damage each did, turrets they built included, with at least a tenth each. On top of the XP for the kills, wave n pays 200 × n XP, 150 × n ore and 40 × n MH. Wave 10 pays double that, 4,000 XP, 3,000 ore and 800 MH, and a rare blueprint to each fighter.

Changed by the balance pass on 15 October: a wave now pays 80 × n XP, 60 × n ore and 16 × n MH, 0.4 of the figures above; wave 10 still pays double. See [the balance post](https://ringshadow.com/blog/balance).

One of the worker's pictures was meant to show Gloamwings meeting the AA towers' fire; the fire is there but the Gloamwings aren't in frame, so it isn't in the album.


---

# The Dropship: no more flying alone

> The Prospector no longer flies by itself. Pilots build Landing Pads and ride the Dropship between them: board, lift off, bank under the ringed giant, dash through cloud and land in another region, 16 to 20 seconds and never a fade.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/blog/dropship

15 October 2026 · M8 · The realm under siege

The Prospector used to jump from pad to pad on its own. I wanted a ship to carry it instead, and now one does: you build a Landing Pad, call the Dropship, walk up its ramp and watch the flight to the other side of the world, with no loading screen and no fade.

![The Dropship banking through cloud, the ringed gas giant filling the sky behind it](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/dropship/cover.jpg)

*The second banking turn, with Ringshadow filling the sky.*

## Landing Pads

Flights go only between Landing Pads that pilots have built, and only to regions you've already been to. A Landing Pad is a building from level 1: its blueprint is 80 ore at the Citadel's shop and it costs 60 ore to build. A region can have two, and like every building they're the realm's, so any pilot uses any pad. The pads in the region files are where new pilots arrive; nobody flies to those.

A flight costs 10 MH plus 5 for each step across the map's grid, so 15 MH to the next region over. From a Spacedock, the big pad, it costs half. With the Ringwalker skill it's free and 30% faster. The old Homing beacon skill, which flew you home, is retired: pilots who had it get their points back and a Landing Pad blueprint.

## The flight

Stand on a pad and press M to pick the pad you're going to. The Dropship comes down onto your pad, seen from a low camera, and the Prospector walks up its ramp. It lifts off in a ring of dust, banks twice with the ringed giant filling the sky, dashes through streaking cloud, swings wide onto the target pad, and you step out. The whole trip is 16 to 20 seconds; a longer trip only makes the dash longer.

The change of region happens during the approach, and drawing it takes 1.6 ms. Frames through the whole flight run 10.8 ms at the median and 12.2 ms at the 95th percentile.

## Prospect Landing to Cold Fork

- ![The world map at a Landing Pad, Landing Pad 1 in Cold Fork picked, FLY for 15 MH](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/dropship/01-menu.webp) On a pad, M: Landing Pad 1 in Cold Fork, for 15 MH.
- ![The Dropship descending on its thrusters, the gas giant behind it](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/dropship/02-descend.webp) The Dropship comes down.
- ![The Dropship on the pad in a cloud of dust as the Prospector boards](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/dropship/03-board.webp) Boarding.
- ![Lift-off in a ring of dust, the giant and its rings behind](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/dropship/04-liftoff.webp) Lift-off in a ring of dust.
- ![The Dropship banking hard in front of the giant](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/dropship/05-turn.webp) Banking under the giant.
- ![The Dropship dashing through bright streaking cloud](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/dropship/06-dash.webp) The dash, through cloud.
- ![The Dropship swinging wide on its approach between clouds](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/dropship/07-approach.webp) The wide approach.
- ![The Dropship settling on the pad in Cold Fork in a cloud of dust](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/dropship/08-step-out.webp) Down on the pad in Cold Fork.
- ![The Prospector on the pad in Cold Fork, the region banner COLD FORK, THE RIDGE](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/dropship/09-landed.webp) Stepped out: Cold Fork.

## What isn't right yet

The first call in a session still stalls once, for 522 ms, the first time the ship is drawn. That's in the editor build; it hasn't been checked in a packaged one yet.

Every test suite passes: 496 core, 254 server and 85 network.

# The Fork: the first canyon to hold

> The first canyon in Ringshadow's world: The Fork in Cold Fork, two winding arms from Brood tunnels to a prize of 36,000 ore and 6,000 MH, with 12 build spots on the rims for the turrets that will hold it.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/blog/the-fork

15 October 2026 · M8 · The realm under siege

The canyon from the [plan a day ago](https://ringshadow.com/blog/defences) has been cut. It's called The Fork, it's in Cold Fork, and it's built for tower defence: the Brood comes out of tunnels at one end, the ore it wants is at the other, and the rims between are where pilots will put their guns. The waves come next.

![The Fork from above: a mesa cut by two winding canyon arms that meet at a basin with deposits round a well, yellow build spots along the rims, the old derrick ruin between the arms](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-fork/cover.jpg)

*The Fork from above. The yellow rings on the rims are the build spots.*

## How it's laid out

The Fork is a mesa in the north-east of Cold Fork. Two arms wind down through it to the canyon floor, each starting at a Brood tunnel, one in the north wall and one in the east. They meet at a basin, and the prize is there: six deposits of 6,000 ore each round an MH well of 6,000. The richest deposit anywhere else in the region holds 3,600.

Ramps lead up to three rims with 12 build spots, marked in amber, overlooking the bends. The old derrick ruin stands on the rim between the arms. A gorge lets pilots walk down onto the floor, so they can fight with their own torches too.

- 2: arms, each from a Brood tunnel to the prize
- 36,000: ore in six deposits, and 6,000 MH in the well
- 12: build spots on three rims
- about 6 s: for a bug to walk 18 cells from tunnel to prize

## Down in The Fork

- ![From a rim: a build spot in the foreground, the canyon arm below, more spots along the far rim](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-fork/02-from-a-rim.webp) From a rim: a build spot over the arm below.
- ![From the canyon floor looking up at a bend, stepped walls, build spot lamps on the rim above](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-fork/03-floor.webp) From the floor, up at a bend. The lamps on top mark the spots.
- ![A Brood tunnel: a dark hollow framed by rock at the foot of the canyon wall](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-fork/04-tunnel.webp) A Brood tunnel, where the waves will come from.
- ![Shardlings on the prize: rich deposits in a ring round an MH well at the junction](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-fork/05-prize.webp) Shardlings sent down a path, already on the prize.
- ![Three build spots on a rim beside a tunnel's mouth](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-fork/06-build-spots.webp) Build spots by a tunnel's mouth.
- ![The world map of Cold Fork, The Fork in its north-east corner](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-fork/07-map.webp) Cold Fork on the [map](https://ringshadow.com/blog/world-map), The Fork top right.

## How it's built

Region files can now cut canyons, with stepped walls and a darker floor, and they can hold zones: a zone has its tunnels, the paths from each tunnel to the prize, the prize's deposits and well, and the build spots. The region tool checks all of it: that every path runs on open floor joined to the rest, that each tunnel stands at the foot of a wall, that the spots and the prize lie inside the zone. On the plan below the red lines are the Brood's paths.

Bugs sent down a path walk it from the tunnel to the prize, 18 cells in 6 to 6.7 seconds, never more than 1.4 cells off the line, and start mining when they get there.

## The plan

- ![The region tool's preview of Cold Fork: the zone The Fork outlined in the north-east, two red paths from the tunnels to the prize, numbered build spots](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-fork/08-plan.webp) The region tool's preview of Cold Fork, The Fork outlined top right.

Every test suite passes: 494 core, 249 server and 85 network.

### Coming ([landed since](https://ringshadow.com/blog/canyon-game))

The waves. The first wave replays until the pilots beat it, then they grow harder, each paying the pilots who fought. If a wave carries off too much of the prize, [the Matriarch](https://ringshadow.com/blog/matriarch) comes out of her nest and fells every turret in The Fork, and it starts again from wave one.


---

# Valleys, not tiles: the regions reshaped

> Ringshadow's nine regions reshaped as natural basins: bays, rock spurs, necks, islands of rock, terraced walls and passages that narrow like canyon mouths, with one high land of rock running between them.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/blog/valleys

15 October 2026 · M8 · The realm under siege

After the regions got [walls and passages](https://ringshadow.com/blog/passages), they still looked like what they are underneath: nine squares in a grid. Now each one is a basin with a shape of its own, and from above the high ground runs on between them as one land.

![Looking into a bay: banded canyon walls stepping down with a shelf halfway up, ore deposits on the grass at their foot](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/valleys/cover.jpg)

*Into a bay: the wall steps down with a shelf halfway up.*

## A shape for each region

A new tool draws the shapes, and it's in the repo with the rest. Each region is now a natural basin taking 50 to 66% of its square. Bays cut 10 to 30% into the land, rock spurs push out between them, and where two bays face each other the land pinches into a neck. Three regions have islands of rock in the middle that the land runs round. No straight run of wall is longer than about 12 to 15 cells, and every passage narrows toward its gap like the mouth of a canyon.

For each region the tool tries 40 shapes, checks that every pad, deposit and site can still be reached on foot from the landing pad, and keeps the valid one with the shortest straight wall. Deposits the walls would have swallowed move onto the land nearby.

The walls step: along stretches of them there's a shelf a few cells wide halfway up, then the rest of the climb. Their tops share one rock colour across the whole world, whatever the ground below, so on the map the high land reads as one piece with basins cut into it.

## From above, before and after

- ![Before: the world map, nine regions as nine filled squares](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/valleys/01-map-before.webp) Before: nine squares.
- ![After: the world map, each region an irregular basin inside one stretch of rocky high ground](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/valleys/02-map-after.webp) After: nine basins in one land.
- ![Before: the nine regions seen at an angle, each filling its square](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/valleys/03-grid-before.webp) Before, seen at an angle.
- ![After: the same nine regions, bays, spurs and islands of rock in each](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/valleys/04-grid-after.webp) After: bays, spurs and islands.

## On the ground

- ![Banded canyon walls stepping down into a bay, a shelf halfway up](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/valleys/05-bay.webp) A bay, with its shelf.
- ![Walking along a wall that bends out of sight, the far side of the basin beyond](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/valleys/06-wall.webp) Along a wall: it bends before it gets long.
- ![The passage out of Prospect Landing between two banded walls, Tern Ridge beyond](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/valleys/07-passage-start.webp) The passage from Prospect Landing.
- ![The same passage from Tern Ridge, the start's beacon beyond](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/valleys/08-passage-tern-ridge.webp) The same passage from Tern Ridge.

## The nest is back

Two bugs came in with the walls, and both are fixed. [The Matriarch's](https://ringshadow.com/blog/matriarch) nest mound had stopped drawing, and a black slab stood near her in Slag Pockets. Both had one cause: a set of ground built away from the world's origin placed its scenery twice, the second copy offset.

## Slag Pockets, fixed

- ![The Matriarch's nest seen from the pad in Slag Pockets, the mound drawn again](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/valleys/09-nest.webp) The nest from the pad, its mound back.
- ![The Matriarch felled at her nest, no black slab in the view](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/valleys/10-down.webp) Her fall, with no slab in the way.

## The crossing, measured again

Walking from Tern Ridge into Prospect Landing on the new shapes, frames ran 11.6 ms at the median, and the longest at the moment of the crossing was 13.2 ms. The walk held between 4.55 and 4.99 cells a second against 4.79 before it, and the camera's largest step was 0.08 cells.

Every test suite passes: 494 core, 241 server and 85 network.


---

# A quieter HUD: the same moments, before and after

> Ringshadow's HUD, decluttered: one lane of toasts at the upper left, one banner slot under the compass, a contract panel a third of its old height, and the same moments before and after.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/blog/hud

15 October 2026 · M8 · The realm under siege

Every feature this week brought its own message: goals, missions, contracts, raids, starfalls, the Matriarch. They all landed in the middle of the screen, on top of the Prospector and on top of each other. Now each kind of message has one place to go.

![A raid on the Citadel: the banner BROOD SWARM under the compass, two small toasts at the upper left, the Prospector's view clear](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/hud/cover.jpg)

*A raid now: one banner under the compass, the rest at the upper left, the middle clear.*

## Where things go now

Toasts go in one lane at the upper left, three at most; the rest wait their turn. The same news arriving twice is merged into one, and unloads add up, so a run of deliveries reads "+72 ORE · 9 TO THE REALM" instead of a stack of small ones.

The big moments get one banner slot under the compass: a level-up, a raid warning, the Matriarch down, a region's name when you arrive. They come one at a time, and they wait while a screen like the Journal or the map is open, so you don't miss one behind it.

The contract panel is one line of titles plus the NEXT line, 52 points tall where it was 158. It opens in full only when there's news about a contract. The Matriarch's boss bar is a compact plate under the compass. The Q, C and G slots moved to the left of the Prospector and the supplies to its right. And a finished job no longer says "CONTRACT DONE: CONTRACT".

## Before and after

- ![Before: a goal, a mission and a contract done all at once, stacked in the middle of the screen over the Prospector](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/hud/01-busy-before.webp) Before: a goal, a mission and a contract finishing at once, stacked on the Prospector.
- ![After: the same moment, the three messages small at the upper left, the contract panel one line](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/hud/02-busy-after.webp) After: the same moment, at the upper left. The panel is one line.
- ![Before: a raid, with the BROOD SWARM banner, a starfall warning, ore and a survey chip all overlapping mid-screen](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/hud/03-raid-before.webp) Before: a raid, a starfall and a delivery on top of each other.
- ![After: BROOD SWARM alone under the compass, the starfall warning and the ore in the lane](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/hud/04-raid-after.webp) After: the raid gets the banner, the rest go in the lane.

- ![After: the boss bar a compact plate under the compass, the banner KSTR: BROOD SWARM under it](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/hud/06-boss-after.webp) After: a compact plate, with the raid banner under it.
- ![Before: the level-up banner with the contract panel open beside it](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/hud/07-level-before.webp) Before: a level-up.
- ![After: the level-up banner under the compass, the panel one line](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/hud/08-level-after.webp) After: the same level-up.
- ![Before: the contract panel at its old height](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/hud/09-panel-before.webp) Before: the contract panel, 158 points tall.
- ![After: the contract panel as one line of titles and the NEXT line](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/hud/10-panel-after.webp) After: 52 points.

## The XP that wasn't missing

The same pass looked into a 200 XP gap in the level bar. It turned out to be a 6 that looked like an 8 at 12 points. The digits are 13 points now.

Every test suite passes: 494 core, 241 server and 85 network.
