# “I reached level 10, now what?”

> After the first ten minutes, KSTR now keeps one goal in front of every Ringshadow pilot, from a chain of 15 picked by level and by what the pilot has done, from pumping MH at level 3 to the Matriarch at 35.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/blog/now-what

15 October 2026 · M8 · The realm under siege

That's what I asked after playing to level 10. The first ten minutes walk you through landing, mining and your first Citadel, and then the game went quiet. Now the radio keeps one goal in front of you, always the next useful thing for your level.

![PROSPECTOR LEVEL 10 banner, with the KSTR toast NEXT: SOMETHING FOR Q under it](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/now-what/cover.jpg)

*Level 10, and the radio already has the next goal: put a skill on Q.*

## One goal at a time

KSTR, the station on your radio, walks a chain of 15 goals in order and shows you the first one you haven't done that your level allows. A goal you've already met when its turn comes is passed without a word, so a pilot who found its own way never gets told to do what it did. When the next goal needs a higher level, KSTR says so ("Reach level 15") and names what that level opens.

The goal isn't a contract. It sits beside the three daily contracts and the Citadel's missions, it never blocks anything, and it pays a little when you do it: about three minutes of play in XP at your level, and 5 MH plus your level.

- Level 3: pump MH at a Derrick.
- Any level: spend your skill points, sign up for a mission at the Citadel, buy something at its shop.
- Level 5: a [gatling gun](https://ringshadow.com/blog/turrets) by your ore, and a [mercenary](https://ringshadow.com/blog/mercenaries).
- Level 8: a Hab Dome in another region.
- Level 10: a skill on Q, a Sentinel to watch the sky, and the hunt for the Foundry's blueprint.
- Level 15: light the Foundry and make a module.
- Level 25: the Lab. Level 35: the Spacedock, and [the Matriarch](https://ringshadow.com/blog/matriarch).

Buildings the realm can only have one of count when any pilot has built them, and a build goal counts as met when the realm is already at its limit, so you're never handed a goal you can't do.

## On screen

- ![The PROSPECTOR LEVEL 10 banner and the toast KSTR · NEXT: SOMETHING FOR Q](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/now-what/01-level-10.webp) Level 10: "Put a skill with a button on Q; the tree marks which ones."
- ![The Journal with a gold NEXT section on top: Something for Q, its pay and why it matters](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/now-what/02-journal.webp) The Journal (L) opens with the goal on top, in gold: what, why, and the pay.
- ![The toast KSTR · NEXT: PUMP SOME SILVER beside the contracts panel](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/now-what/03-pump.webp) The first goal after the opening: put a Derrick on a well and fill one tank.
- ![The toast KSTR · NEXT: SPEND YOUR POINTS](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/now-what/04-points.webp) "You're sitting on 2 skill points. KSTR can't spend them for you, and they don't earn interest."
- ![GOAL DONE: SPEND YOUR POINTS, +240 XP and +10 MH, and the next goal, SIGN UP AT THE CITADEL](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/now-what/05-goal-done.webp) Done: +240 XP and +10 MH at level 4, and the next goal comes at once.
- ![The whole contract panel with the NEXT line at its foot](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/now-what/06-panel.webp) The NEXT line sits at the foot of the contracts panel.

## Where it shows

A gold NEXT line sits under your contracts. A new goal arrives as a toast with KSTR's line, and a goal with a place, like the nearest well with MH or the Citadel, gets a KSTR mark on the world map, the minimap and the compass. The Journal opens with the goal on top. The lines are text for now; narration can come later, as it did for the missions.

Every test suite passes: 488 core, 241 server and 85 network.


---

# The Brood, painted: before and after the art pass

> The art pass on Ringshadow's Brood: veined egg shells lit from within, opal chitin that shifts colour with the view, glass wings, the Matriarch's glowing sac and crown, and the gatling gun painted from its forge concept. Before and after.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/blog/brood-art

15 October 2026 · M8 · The realm under siege

The Brood went into the world as blockouts: the right shapes and sizes, in flat colours. Every post since has said an art pass was queued. It has landed, and the pictures below are the same scenes before and after.

![The Matriarch at her nest after the art pass: her sac and egg pods glowing violet with pale veins, teal tips on her crown](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/brood-art/cover.jpg)

*The Matriarch roaring at her nest, after the pass.*

## Three new materials

Most of the change comes from three materials the whole Brood now shares. The egg shell is veined and lit from within. The opal chitin is dark plates with a sheen of teal, violet and gold that moves as the view does. The glass is translucent, for wings and sacs. The paintings from [the day the Brood was designed](https://ringshadow.com/blog/the-brood) were the reference.

The Matriarch's sac and egg pods glow with veins now, and her crown has a violet membrane between the spines, with teal tips. Her nest is a tiered mound with glowing seams of ore and clusters of opal. Shardlings have opal quills. Gloamwings have veined wings of violet glass and a lit lantern. A Lodeback carries a glass sac lit gold, with dark ore packed round a gold heart.

## The Brood, before and after

- ![Before: the Matriarch's model with a flat pink sac and flat pink pods](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/brood-art/01-queen-before.webp) Before: her sac and pods in flat pink.
- ![After: the Matriarch's sac a glossy violet shell with pale veins, her pods clustered and lit](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/brood-art/02-queen-after.webp) After: veined shell, lit from within.
- ![Before: a Lodeback with a flat yellow sac, a Gloamwing and a Shardling in plain colours](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/brood-art/03-brood-before.webp) Before: Lodeback, Gloamwing, Shardling.
- ![After: the Lodeback's sac gold glass with ore inside, the Gloamwing's wings violet glass, the Shardling's quills opal](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/brood-art/04-brood-after.webp) After: the gold glass sac, glass wings, opal quills.
- ![Before: the Matriarch roaring at her nest, her body flat black and pink](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/brood-art/05-roar-before.webp) Before: the roar.
- ![After: the same roar, her sac and pods glowing violet with veins, the nest in tiers](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/brood-art/06-roar-after.webp) After: the same roar.
- ![Before: the nest seen from the pad in Slag Pockets, the Matriarch a dark shape with pink spots](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/brood-art/07-nest-before.webp) Before: the nest from the pad.
- ![After: the nest from the pad, the Matriarch's crown and pods glowing over the rim](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/brood-art/08-nest-after.webp) After: the crown and pods read across the slag.

## The guns too

The pass covered the [defences](https://ringshadow.com/blog/turrets) as well. The gatling gun is painted from its forge concept now: a tall furnace hopper of molten amalgam with glowing slits, over a ribbed gunmetal jacket. The Citadel's corner turrets are 1.8 times bigger, with lit rings at the muzzle. The amalgam rounds are drawn as a white-hot core in an orange halo, and they throw bigger sparks where they hit. The upgrade chevrons on a turret's base glow in their stats' colours: amber, red, ice and blue.

## The gatling gun, before and after

- ![Before: the gatling gun as a grey blockout box firing at a Shardling](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/brood-art/11-gatling-before.webp) Before: the blockout, firing at a swarm.
- ![After: the painted gatling gun with its furnace hopper, rounds streaking into a Shardling](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/brood-art/12-gatling-after.webp) After: the forge, with its rounds drawn.
- ![Before: an upgraded gatling gun with white chevrons on its base](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/brood-art/15-chevrons-before.webp) Before: the upgrade chevrons in plain white.
- ![After: the same gun painted, its chevrons glowing amber, red, ice and blue](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/brood-art/16-chevrons-after.webp) After: each stat in its own colour.

## What it costs

Glowing, see-through materials cost more to draw. With 18 to 22 bugs in sight, the GPU's median frame went from 10.12 to 10.42 ms, about 0.3 ms more. The whole frame averages 10.52 ms, and its 95th percentile is 11.16 ms, well inside the 16.7 ms a frame at 60 a second allows.

## What isn't right yet

The nest's mound stopped drawing when the regions got their walls, so the nest pictures here were taken before that change. The fix is part of the next pass on the regions' outlines, and [it has landed since](https://ringshadow.com/blog/valleys). The Citadel's corner turrets are bigger now, but from the usual camera they still read small.


---

# Through the walls: walking between regions

> Ringshadow's regions now have grounds of their own, cliff walls and 14 passages between them, and walking from one region into the next happens without a reload or a jump.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/blog/passages

15 October 2026 · M8 · The realm under siege

The world is nine regions, each run by the server on its own. Until now you could tell where one stopped: the ground looked the same everywhere, and the edge was a line. Now each region has a ground of its own, walls of cliff around it and passages through them, and you walk from one into the next without anything moving or reloading.

![A passage between two cliff walls, seen from Prospect Landing, the next region's ground visible through the gap](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/passages/cover.jpg)

*A passage out of Prospect Landing, with Tern Ridge through the gap.*

## A ground for each region

Arriving somewhere new should look like it. Prospect Landing and Tern Ridge keep the brown dirt. Rust Hollow is rust-red earth with darker iron stains. Brine Pans is pale salt crust in plates, grey brine in the cracks. Ashen Shelf is soft grey ash. Glass Flats is dark glassy ground in facets that catch the sun. Slag Pockets, where [the Matriarch](https://ringshadow.com/blog/matriarch) nests, is black slag with cracks that glow like embers. Cold Fork has frost on its stone until mid-morning, and Dust Terraces has ochre in bands by height.

The last 16 cells before each edge blend halfway toward the neighbour's ground, so both sides of a border meet in the same colour.

## The nine grounds

- ![Nine regions from above in a grid: Ashen Shelf, Cold Fork, Glass Flats; Rust Hollow, Prospect Landing, Tern Ridge; Dust Terraces, Brine Pans, Slag Pockets](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/passages/01-palettes.webp) Top row: Ashen Shelf, Cold Fork, Glass Flats. Middle: Rust Hollow, Prospect Landing, Tern Ridge. Bottom: Dust Terraces, Brine Pans, Slag Pockets.

## Walls, and the ways through them

Each region now has a border: the outline of its playable land, with cliff walls rising outside it, rock-strewn on top. Nothing walks on the walls. Fourteen passages cut through them across the world, and each one is laid out on both sides at the same floor height, so the gap you see from one region lines up with the gap on the other.

## Walls and passages

- ![Looking down over a cliff wall into a grey region, rocks and spires along the wall's top](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/passages/02-over-the-wall.webp) Over the wall into a grey-grounded region, its rim strewn with rock.
- ![A banded cliff wall seen from the ground inside a region](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/passages/03-wall-inside.webp) The wall from the inside.
- ![The passage seen from Prospect Landing, a pad in the foreground](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/passages/04-passage-start.webp) The passage from Prospect Landing…
- ![The same passage seen from Tern Ridge, the start's beacon of light visible beyond it](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/passages/05-passage-tern-ridge.webp) …and the same passage from Tern Ridge, with the start's beacon beyond it.

## Crossing without a seam

Each region has its own simulation on the server. When a unit walks up to an open edge, the server hands it to the neighbour at exactly the same point. The client keeps one world frame for everything and builds the neighbouring region's ground ahead of you, so at the moment you cross nothing moves, nothing reloads and the camera doesn't jump. The other way to do it, shifting the whole world's origin to the new region, cost 20 to 27 ms a crossing when it was measured, longer than a frame.

Measured on a walk from Tern Ridge into Prospect Landing:

- 13.2 ms: the longest frame at the crossing; 13.1 ms is a normal 95th percentile
- 4.63: cells a second, the walk before the crossing; 4.55 to 4.95 in each frame round it
- 0.08: cells, the camera's largest step
- 0.05: cells, the most the walk strayed from its line

## Walking through

- ![The Prospector in Tern Ridge, walking toward the passage between two cliff walls](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/passages/06-walk-1.webp) In Tern Ridge, heading for the passage.
- ![The Prospector between the cliff walls of the passage](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/passages/07-walk-2.webp) Between the walls.
- ![The Prospector past the walls, open ground ahead](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/passages/08-walk-3.webp) Through the gap.
- ![The Prospector in Prospect Landing, the beacon ahead](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/passages/09-walk-4.webp) Over the edge: now in Prospect Landing.
- ![The banner PROSPECT LANDING, Open Field, shown as the Prospector arrives](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/passages/10-walk-5.webp) The region's name is the only sign you crossed.

## What isn't right yet

From above, the regions still read as rectangles: their walls follow the cells' edges in long straight runs. A second pass that gives each region an irregular outline is next ([it has landed since](https://ringshadow.com/blog/valleys)), and after it the first canyon gets cut into a region for the [turrets](https://ringshadow.com/blog/turrets) to hold.

Every test suite passes: 488 core, 233 server and 84 network, and all nine regions validate.


---

# The world map: the real ground, seen from above

> Press M and Ringshadow's world map shows every region you've been to as a picture of its real ground from above, with live pilots, mercenaries, the Brood, buildings and deposits, and a tooltip on each.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/blog/world-map

15 October 2026 · M8 · The realm under siege

The map on M used to be a drawing: flat colours, one per region. Now it's a picture of the actual ground taken from straight above, with everything that's alive drawn over it, and you can point at any of it to ask what it is.

![The world map: nine regions in a three by three grid, each a top-down picture of its ground, from grey ash and glittering glass to rust, salt and slag](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/world-map/cover.jpg)

*The whole world on M, after the regions got their own grounds.*

## A photograph of every region

Each region is baked into one picture. The game builds the region the way a client would and photographs it with a camera pointing straight down: its terrain, cliffs, rocks and plants, its ore and wells, lit at half past ten in the morning in clear weather, with no units and no fog. That's 8 pixels a cell, 1152 × 768 for a medium region, north up. A script does the whole world in two hidden runs, so when a region changes the map is rebaked in one command.

The pictures lie side by side as the regions do. A region you haven't been to stays dark, with its outline and its name, UNCHARTED. The map opens centred on you; the wheel zooms, dragging pans, and the world keeps running while it's open.

## The map, twice

- ![The world map when it first landed: six regions in desert colours, three still dark and UNCHARTED](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/world-map/01-world-m2.webp) When it landed: six regions seen, three still uncharted, before each region had a ground of its own.
- ![The world map rebaked: all nine regions, each in its own ground](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/world-map/02-world-palettes.webp) Rebaked a few hours later, once each region had a [ground of its own](https://ringshadow.com/blog/passages).
- ![Zoomed in on Prospect Landing: the Citadel, pads, deposits in violet, plants and cliffs](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/world-map/03-prospect-landing.webp) Zoomed in on Prospect Landing. Violet marks are deposits, the rings are pads.

## What's alive on it

Over the pictures the map draws what's happening now: you as a cyan arrow, other pilots, your mercenaries in orange, the Brood in red groups with their count, the realm's buildings, deposits in violet that shrink as they empty, MH wells, the blueprint sites you know of in gold, pads as yellow rings, starfalls and their craters, the missions in your Journal and the ringshadow band while it sweeps across. Live units, buildings and deposits show only in the region you're in. Elsewhere the map shows what you know: sites, pads, missions, and your mercenaries at their fields.

Point at anything and a tooltip says what's worth knowing. A deposit shows how much ore is left, and whether a Lodeback is eating it. A building shows who built it and its HP. A site shows its blueprint and whether it's been opened. A mission shows its tier and instructions, and a mercenary its field and what it has delivered. Clicking a mission or a site points your compass at it.

## Tooltips

- ![The map with a tooltip on an ore deposit](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/world-map/04-tip-deposit.webp) A deposit and the ore left in it.
- ![The map with a tooltip on the Citadel: Built by you, HP 1,500 of 1,500](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/world-map/05-tip-building.webp) The Citadel: built by you, HP 1,500 of 1,500.
- ![The map with a tooltip on a mission marker: Mark the Ground, an easy survey mission in Prospect Landing](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/world-map/06-tip-mission.webp) Mark the Ground, an easy survey mission. Click it to steer the compass there.
- ![The map with a tooltip on a mercenary named Zinc, working field 2 in Prospect Landing](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/world-map/07-tip-merc.webp) Zinc, a [mercenary](https://ringshadow.com/blog/mercenaries), just hired: field 2, nothing delivered yet.

## What isn't right yet

The pictures show the regions as near rectangles, because that's still how they read from above: their walls run along the cells' edges. A second pass on the outlines is next, and the map will be rebaked after it. [Both have landed since.](https://ringshadow.com/blog/valleys)

The test suites passed when it landed: 473 core, 216 server and 81 network.


---

# The Matriarch wakes in Slag Pockets

> The Brood's queen now lives at her nest in Slag Pockets: 6,000 hp, a slam, an acid spit and a roar that rallies her horde. Pilots who bring her down share 3,000 ore, 1,500 MH and a rare blueprint.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/blog/matriarch

15 October 2026 · M8 · The realm under siege

The Brood has a queen now. She lives at her nest in Slag Pockets, two regions from the start, with her horde around her, and she's the first thing in the world a pilot can't beat alone.

![The Matriarch rearing in her roar over her nest, Shardlings at her feet, her boss bar at the top of the screen](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/matriarch/cover.jpg)

*She roars when a pilot first comes close, and every 30 seconds in a fight.*

## Her nest

The nest sits on the east plateau of Slag Pockets, 50 cells from the region's pad. It's a ring mound of chitin plates, dark rock and opal ore, 12 cells across, with egg pods on its flanks and seven spines around the rim. She stands in its bowl. She's 9.5 cells tall and her crown of spines glows violet, so you can see her over the rim from 55 cells away across the slag.

Her horde keeps the nest: four packs of Shardlings, 16 to 24 in all, and 4 to 8 Gloamwings over her. A new one hatches every 20 seconds while the nest is short. A pack goes for any pilot who steps into its patch and chases it anywhere inside the nest's 30-cell ring.

## From the painting to the plateau

- ![Concept painting of the nest: a ring mound of black chitin with curved spines round its rim and clusters of glowing violet egg pods](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/matriarch/01-nest-concept.webp) The nest's concept: a mound of chitin, spines on the rim, egg pods on the flanks.
- ![The Prospector on a pad in Slag Pockets, the Matriarch's glowing crown visible far off over the nest's rim, Shardlings in between](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/matriarch/02-nest-afar.webp) From the pad in Slag Pockets: her crown over the nest, her packs in between.

## How she fights

- 6,000: hp, with armour 3: the Prospector's torch does 2 a strike
- 40 / 60: her slam to units and to buildings, every 4 s
- 12 cells: her acid spit's range, at the ground or the air
- ×1.3: her horde's speed for 10 s after a roar

She slams: both forelimbs rise for 0.8 seconds and crash down on everything on the ground within 3 cells in front of her. She spits acid every 3 seconds, 18 to a unit or 30 to a building, and it leaves a burning puddle 2 cells wide for 4 seconds. She roars once when a pilot first comes within 25 cells, then every 30 seconds while she fights. The roar sends every bug of her nest within 40 cells after her target at a third more speed, hatches four more Shardlings from her pods, is heard across the whole region and faintly in the next, and shakes the view of anyone close. She never goes more than 6 cells from the nest's centre, and after 20 seconds without a hit she mends 20 hp a second.

Near her, or once she's hurt, a boss bar shows at the top of the screen with her 6,000 hp.

A pilot alone can't take her down with the torch: 2 damage a strike against 6,000 hp, while she mends. What brings her down is turrets the realm builds at the nest, the [gatling guns and Sentinels](https://ringshadow.com/blog/turrets), and several pilots at once.

## The fight

- ![The Matriarch rearing in her roar, the boss bar THE MATRIARCH full at the top](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/matriarch/03-roar.webp) The roar: she rears for 2 seconds and the nest turns on you.
- ![Close up, the Matriarch's forelimbs crashing down on the Prospector, the screen edged in red](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/matriarch/04-slam.webp) Under the slam. The red edge is the Prospector taking the hit.
- ![The Matriarch at her nest with the boss bar showing about half her health](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/matriarch/05-boss-bar.webp) The boss bar at half.
- ![The Matriarch fallen, with the toasts THE MATRIARCH IS DOWN and YOUR SHARE OF THE MATRIARCH: 3,000 ore, 1,500 MH, a Bastion blueprint](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/matriarch/06-down.webp) Down, felled by one pilot in this staged shot: the whole share, 3,000 ore, 1,500 MH and a Bastion blueprint.

## Her fall, and her return

When she falls, every pilot in the world hears "THE MATRIARCH IS DOWN". Every pilot who hurt her, with its Prospector or with a turret it built, gets a share of 3,000 ore and 1,500 MH by the damage it did (5% at least), and one rare blueprint copy, one of the three with the highest level floors. XP goes the same way, by each hit's share of her 6,000 hp. Her horde scatters with every other bug in the region, and no new group comes for a world day.

She doesn't stay down. Three world days after her fall, two hours on the world's clock, every pilot hears "THE MATRIARCH STIRS" and the nest starts to grow back from empty, one hatchling every 20 seconds. That's saved with the world, so it holds across restarts.

The Citadel's mission board knows about her too: one perilous hunt in three is "The Matriarch", and its marker is her nest.

## What isn't right yet

Her egg pods still read as flat pink shapes in the pictures, nothing like the glowing pods in the painting. An art pass on her and the rest of the Brood is queued. [It has landed since.](https://ringshadow.com/blog/brood-art)

Every test suite passes: 488 core, 233 server and 84 network.

### Coming

The canyon. When pilots lose a wave there, she's the one who comes: she walks out of her nest with an escort, fells every Sentinel and gatling gun in the zone, and the canyon starts over from wave one. The server can already send her; the waves that call her are next.


---

# Guns for the realm: the Citadel shoots back

> The Citadel now shoots back with four corner turrets, pilots build a Sentinel AA tower and a gatling gun firing red-hot ore-and-MH rounds, and every placed turret takes upgrades paid from your own wallet.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/blog/turrets

15 October 2026 · M8 · The realm under siege

Since the Brood arrived, a pilot could only fight them with the Prospector's torch, and the torch was never meant to win a fight. Now the realm has guns: four on the Citadel, two kinds you build yourself, and upgrades for each one.

![A swarm of Shardlings and two Gloamwings heading for the Citadel at Prospect Landing, with the KSTR warning BROOD SWARM, heading for the Citadel](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/turrets/cover.jpg)

*KSTR warns of a swarm heading for the Citadel. Its corner turrets will meet it.*

## The Citadel fires back

Every Citadel now has four point-defence turrets, one on each corner pylon. They come with the building, cost nothing and need no blueprint. Each one is a rotary close-in gun that fires at bugs on the ground and in the air from 7.5 cells. One turret kills a Shardling in 2 seconds, and the four together clear a raid of eight Shardlings and three Gloamwings in about 10.

Their upgrades sit on a new DEFENCE tab at the Citadel (H). There are three marks each for fire rate (+20%), damage (+25%) and range (+1 cell). They're paid from the realm wallet, the one the [10% tax](https://ringshadow.com/blog/the-realm) fills: 250 ore for a first mark, then 500 ore and 50 MH, then 1,000 ore and 150 MH. Any pilot can buy them, and everyone who unloads at the Citadel has helped pay.

## Two turrets you build

The Sentinel is the AA tower, the strategy game's anti-air building brought into the world. Its missile pods shoot only at things in the air, from 7 cells, which is further than a Gloamwing can spit (4). Two volleys kill a Gloamwing. It opens at level 10 and costs 150 ore and 100 MH; the realm can have four.

The gatling gun is new. It fires red-hot rounds of amalgam, ore fused with Metallic Hydrogen, four shots a second for 16 damage a second, at the ground within 6 cells and at the air within 4.5, just past a Gloamwing's spit. A Shardling lasts 1.25 seconds in front of it, a pack of six about 8. It opens at level 5 and costs 125 ore and 25 MH; the realm can have six.

Both need a blueprint copy, like every building. Bugs that get shot turn on the turret that shot them, and whoever built it gets half the XP for the damage it does.

## The guns, in the game

- ![Shardlings and Gloamwings advancing on the Citadel, with the BROOD SWARM warning](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/turrets/01-citadel.webp) A raid on its way to the Citadel. The corner turrets are on its pylons.
- ![The Citadel's DEFENCE tab with three columns: fire rate, damage and range, each with its mark, value and price](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/turrets/02-defence-tab.webp) The DEFENCE tab: fire rate at mark 1, the next mark 500 ore and 50 MH from the realm wallet.
- ![Three Gloamwings hovering over a Sentinel AA tower on a ridge](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/turrets/03-sentinel.webp) Three Gloamwings over a Sentinel.
- ![A Shardling caught in the gatling gun's fire, glowing red, with the warning BROOD SWARM, heading for the Gatling Gun](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/turrets/04-gatling.webp) A swarm comes for the gatling gun. The red one is taking its rounds.
- ![The build menu listing Citadel, Derrick, Gatling Gun, Hab Dome, Sentinel and the rest, with copies held and prices](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/turrets/05-build-menu.webp) The build menu: Gatling Gun 125 ore and 25 MH, Sentinel 150 ore and 100 MH.

## Marks on every turret

Every Sentinel and gatling gun you place takes marks too, three per stat, paid at the turret from your own wallet with no tax. Stand within 4 cells of it and press U: a card opens with the turret's kills and builder, and a column for each stat showing its marks, its value now and next, and the price.

- +20%: fire rate a mark: a gatling's 4 shots a second become 6.4 at mark 3
- +25%: damage a mark: 4 a round to 7
- +1 cell: range a mark: the gatling's ground reach 6 to 9
- 6 cells: the gatling's air reach at mark 3, up from 4.5, still short of the Sentinel's 7

On a gatling gun every stat's marks cost 100 ore and 50 MH, then 300 and 200, then 800 and 500. A fully upgraded gun is 4,800 ore and 3,000 MH, about an hour and a half of pumping MH at a Derrick. A Sentinel costs half as much again per mark. Any pilot can upgrade any turret of the realm, since it defends everyone, and every pilot in the region hears who did. The marks show on the turret itself: a plate of chevrons at the front and back of its base, lit amber for fire rate, ember for damage, ice for range and sky blue for air reach.

A turret that falls loses its marks and its kills, with no refund, and a new one built in its place starts bare. That rule is there for the canyon, where the Matriarch will come to flatten the turrets when the pilots lose a wave.

## The turret card

- ![The gatling gun's card: fire rate mark 1 of 3, damage mark 2, range mark 1, air reach at its last mark, each with an UPGRADE button](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/turrets/07-card.webp) A gatling gun after seven marks: air reach is full at 6 cells, damage's next mark is 800 ore and 500 MH.

## Before and after the marks

- ![A bare gatling gun on a ridge, a Gloamwing hovering out of its reach behind it](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/turrets/06-bare.webp) A bare gatling gun. The Gloamwing behind it hovers out of its 4.5-cell air reach.
- ![The same gatling gun with lit chevrons on the plate at the front of its base](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/turrets/08-chevrons.webp) The same gun after its marks: the chevrons are lit on its base.
- ![The upgraded gatling gun with a Gloamwing, its health bar showing damage, now in range](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/turrets/09-air-reach.webp) With its air reach at 6, the gun hits the same Gloamwing.

## What isn't right yet

The gatling gun in the pictures is a blockout, not the painted forge from the [concept post](https://ringshadow.com/blog/defences). The Citadel's corner turrets read small from the ground, and the amalgam rounds don't draw their tracer streams yet. All three are on the list for the Brood's art pass, which [has landed since](https://ringshadow.com/blog/brood-art). One bug turned up while building the upgrades: the client's pose table had room for nine building kinds, and the gatling gun is the tenth, so its head never turned and its barrels never spun. It's sized from the building list now, and the gun turns and fires.

Every test suite passes: 475 core, 219 server and 82 network.

### Coming

The canyon. Some zones become canyons the Brood attacks in waves along set paths, and pilots hold them with these guns along the rims. Losing a wave brings the Matriarch, who fells every turret in the zone. She's [in the world now](https://ringshadow.com/blog/matriarch), in her nest in Slag Pockets; the canyon and its waves are next.


---

# Mercenaries: they mine while you sleep

> Hire mercenary prospectors at Ringshadow's Citadel: in a world day each one mines what you mine in an hour, and they keep working while the game is closed.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/blog/mercenaries

14 October 2026 · M8 · The realm under siege

The world now runs while the game is closed. So I asked for someone to work it: mercenary prospectors, hired at the Citadel, who dig your ore while you're away.

![A hired Prospector labelled MERC · NETTLE drilling a deposit beside the pilot's own Prospector](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/mercenaries/03-mining.webp)

*MERC · NETTLE at work on a deposit field at Prospect Landing.*

The Citadel's fourth tab is MERCS. On the left are your mercenaries; on the right, the region's deposit fields with the ore left in each. Pick a field, press HIRE, and a Prospector with a name over its head walks out to dig there, then hauls the ore home to the Citadel.

My one rule: in a whole world day, a mercenary mines what you mine in an hour. At level 5 that is 4,860 ore a day. The ore is yours, and like any unload it pays the realm its 10%. It earns you no XP: leveling stays something you do yourself.

- 500: ore and 50 MH for the first hire, doubling for each one after
- 5 + L/5: MH a day in wages, paid at dawn
- 1 · 2 · 3: mercenaries at levels 5, 15 and 30

Wages come out of your MH at every dawn. A mercenary who isn't paid leaves. You can send one to another field or dismiss it from the same tab.

They work with the game closed, because [the world server keeps running](https://ringshadow.com/blog/world-runs-on), and if the Mac was off the server catches up the hours when it starts again. When you come back the game tells you what happened: WHILE YOU WERE AWAY, mercs delivered 747 ore.

## Hire, mine, come back

- ![The Citadel's MERCS tab: two open places, a third opening at level 30, and seven deposit fields](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/mercenaries/01-mercs-tab.webp) The MERCS tab: places for your mercenaries, and the fields they can work.
- ![The MERCS tab after hiring Nettle, with SEND and DISMISS buttons, the next hire at 1,000 ore and 100 MH](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/mercenaries/02-hired.webp) Nettle hired for 500 ore and 50 MH. The next one costs double.
- ![MERC · NETTLE drilling at a deposit](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/mercenaries/03-mining.webp) MERC · NETTLE on the field.
- ![Arriving at Prospect Landing with banners: WHILE YOU WERE AWAY, mercs delivered 747 ore; a research and a module finished](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/mercenaries/04-while-away.webp) Back in the game: the mercs delivered 747 ore, and the Lab and the Foundry finished their jobs too.

The mercenaries have a paint of their own, but it doesn't read well from a distance yet; that's a follow-up. The same task fixed a bug: the TAKE button on the missions board did nothing when clicked. The suites now stand at 467 core tests, 209 server tests and 71 network tests, all passing.

# The world runs on after you quit

> Quit Ringshadow and its world keeps going: the local server stays up on the Mac, the clock turns, meteors fall and the Brood roams, at about 0.008% of a CPU core.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/blog/world-runs-on

14 October 2026 · M8 · The realm under siege

A world that lasts shouldn't stop when you close the game, and now it keeps going. The local server runs on your Mac, and the game picks it back up when you return.

![The home screen with a line reading World server running, since 23:03, and a STOP button](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/world-runs-on/03-home-running.webp)

*The home screen tells you the world is still running, and since when.*

In Ringshadow's online mode the game is only a client. The world lives in a separate server program, the same one a public world will run, and until today it quit with the game. Now it detaches. Quit, and the world's clock keeps turning, starfalls keep coming, the Foundry and the Lab finish their jobs, and the Brood's director keeps sending bugs to the places worth being. Start the game again and it finds the running server and reattaches.

A server that runs all the time had better be cheap. With nobody connected it slows down: the clock and timers tick twice a second, the regions wait, and it costs about 0.008% of one CPU core. With a pilot in the world it runs at the full 60 steps a second, about 0.3 to 0.5%.

If the Mac was off, there's nothing to run on, so the world catches up instead: on the next start the server works through the downtime, up to 24 hours of it. The same catch-up pays the [mercenary prospectors](https://ringshadow.com/blog/mercenaries) you can hire at the Citadel.

The home screen shows "World server running" with the time it started, and a STOP button for when you want it off.

## Quit, come back

- ![The Prospector on its landing pad at Prospect Landing, before the game quits](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/world-runs-on/01-first-run.webp) Before quitting: the Prospector on the pad.
- ![The same spot after the game restarts and reattaches, the clouds moved on](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/world-runs-on/02-reattached.webp) After a restart: same world, same pilot. The clouds moved on while the game was closed.
- ![The home screen showing World server running with a STOP button](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/world-runs-on/03-home-running.webp) World server running, with STOP.
- ![The home screen after STOP, without the server line](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/world-runs-on/04-home-stopped.webp) After STOP: the line is gone.

The network protocol didn't change. The tests stand at 467 core, 200 server and 70 network, all passing, and they never leave a server running behind them.


---

# Coming next: guns for the realm, and a canyon to hold

> What is being built now in Ringshadow: the Citadel's guns, an AA tower, a gatling gun firing red-hot ore-and-MH rounds, and a canyon the pilots defend wave by wave.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/blog/defences

14 October 2026 · M8 · The realm under siege Coming

Nothing on this page is in the game yet. It's what the agents started on tonight, and what I've asked for after it. The posts about each piece will come when it lands.

Since landed: [the guns and their upgrades](https://ringshadow.com/blog/turrets), [the Matriarch](https://ringshadow.com/blog/matriarch), [the satellite map](https://ringshadow.com/blog/world-map), [passages between regions](https://ringshadow.com/blog/passages), [the first canyon](https://ringshadow.com/blog/the-fork), [its waves](https://ringshadow.com/blog/canyon-game) and [the Dropship](https://ringshadow.com/blog/dropship).

![Concept painting of a gatling turret with a glowing furnace hopper on top, firing](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/defences/01-gatling-forge.webp)

*The gatling gun, "forge" concept: a furnace hopper feeding red-hot rounds.*

## The Citadel fires back

The Citadel gets four point-defence turrets, one on each corner, free with the building. They shoot at bugs on their own, and their upgrades for fire rate, damage and range sit on a new DEFENCE tab. They're paid from the realm wallet, the one the [10% tax](https://ringshadow.com/blog/the-realm) fills. So every pilot who unloads helps pay for guns that protect everyone.

## Two turrets you build

The AA tower is the Sentinel, the strategy game's anti-air building, brought into the world. It shoots only at things in the air, from 7 cells, which is further than a Gloamwing can spit (4). It's planned to open at about level 10.

The gatling gun is new: it fires red-hot rounds of amalgam, ore fused with Metallic Hydrogen, at the ground and at close air, so a flock diving on it gets shot. It's planned for about level 5. Three concepts were painted; the worker's pick is the forge, with its glowing furnace hopper, and I still have the last word on it.

After them, turret upgrades: marks for fire rate, damage and range on each AA tower and gatling, paid at the turret from your own wallet and shown on the turret.

## The gatling concepts, and the Sentinel

- ![Gatling concept forge: finned base, ribbed barrel jacket, glowing furnace hopper](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/defences/01-gatling-forge.webp) Forge: finned base, ribbed barrel jacket, a glowing furnace hopper. The worker's pick.
- ![Gatling concept cradle: the gun in an open cradle between two arms, a glowing ammo drum](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/defences/02-gatling-cradle.webp) Cradle: the gun between two arms, a glowing ammo drum.
- ![Gatling concept bunker: an octagonal base, a sloped shield and a side belt box](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/defences/03-gatling-bunker.webp) Bunker: octagonal base, sloped shield, side belt box.
- ![The Sentinel concept: a square bunker with two raised missile pods on a yoke](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/defences/04-sentinel.webp) The Sentinel's concept from 4 October: two missile pods on a yoke. It becomes the AA tower.

## The canyon

The part I'm most curious about is the canyon. Some zones of the world become canyons, and they play as tower defence. The bugs come in waves along set paths through the canyon toward a field of rich ore and MH, to mine it for themselves. Pilots build AA towers and gatling guns along the rims.

- The first wave replays until the pilots beat it, with turrets or with their own torches.
- Beating it starts the zone's game: waves that grow harder, each one paying every pilot who fought in it.
- If a wave carries off too much of the prize, the queen comes. The Matriarch fells every turret in the zone, and it starts over from wave one.
- Clear the last wave and the canyon is held for a world day: the prize field is the pilots' to mine, with no waves.

The first canyon will be cut into a region one step out from the start. The Matriarch herself is on the list too: her nest in Slag Pockets, her slam, her acid and her roar, and a reward for the pilots who bring her down.

## Also on the list

- Regions whose borders follow the land, with passages you can see and drive through without a cut.
- No more solo flights: you build landing pads and ride a Dropship between them.
- The map as a satellite view of the real ground, with tooltips on every site, building and deposit.
- The world keeps running after you quit, as long as the Mac is on, and [mercenary prospectors](https://ringshadow.com/blog/mercenaries) keep mining while you're away (both have landed since).

### How M8 ends

The milestone is done when, in a recorded run, a pilot at Prospect Landing pays the Citadel's tax, buys a blueprint and a supply, builds a gatling gun that kills bugs drawn to a deposit, walks through a passage into the next region, and rides the Dropship from one built pad to another, with every test suite passing.

# The Brood: from a painting to the world in a day

> Ringshadow's first enemies: four alien bugs, from concept paintings to blockout models to the world, where they linger at deposits, bite, dive, eat ore and raid buildings.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/blog/the-brood

14 October 2026 · M8 · The realm under siege

Until this evening nothing on the frontier fought back. You mined and built in peace. Then I asked the agents for something that would come for you.

![A Shardling biting the Prospector, the screen edged red, the bug outlined in red](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-brood/11-attack.webp)

*A Shardling on the Prospector. The red edge means you're being bitten.*

These were my words to the agents:

"I need some enemies while I go around to mine ore and MH. Some alien bugs of some sort, they are always attracted to the POIs in the game. They come, linger around and live, if I am in their site they attack. It could be one, it could be more."

I added that they should attack buildings, eat the ore out of unguarded veins, and that a giant brood queen should live in one of the far regions with a horde around her.

## Four kinds, painted first

An agent designed the family, named it the Brood, and painted three directions for each kind with Grok Imagine, a rest pose and an attack pose side by side. They belong to this world: dark chitin the colour of the ore rock, opal flecks crusted into the shell, and light coming from inside, so at night they are moving lights before they are shapes. Each kind glows in its own colour so you can tell them apart from the high camera. I picked one of the three for each.

## The concepts I picked

- ![Concept painting of the Shardling: a six-legged bug with opal crystal quills glowing teal at the roots](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-brood/01-shardling-concept.webp) Shardling, "quill": the swarmer, opal quills glowing teal.
- ![Concept painting of the Gloamwing: violet wings and a glowing lantern abdomen, spitting acid](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-brood/02-gloamwing-concept.webp) Gloamwing, "lantern": the flyer, a violet light from above.
- ![Concept painting of the Lodeback: a crab-like bug carrying a glassy sac full of opal ore](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-brood/03-lodeback-concept.webp) Lodeback, "hermit": the ore eater, its sac filling with opal.
- ![Concept painting of the Matriarch: a towering armoured queen with a violet spine crown and a glowing egg sac](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-brood/04-matriarch-concept.webp) The Matriarch, "crowned": the queen, with her egg sac.

## What each one does

The numbers are built against the Prospector, which has 45 hp, walks at 3.94 cells a second and fights with a cutting torch: about 4.7 damage a second, at the ground only. The Prospector builds; it fights badly, on purpose.

| Kind | hp | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Shardling | 20 | Packs at deposits, wells, sites and pads. Chases at 4.4, faster than you walk, so you can leave its site but you can't outrun it in the open. Bites for 2 every 1.2 s. |
| Gloamwing | 30 | Flies at rooftop height and spits acid from 4 cells, out of the torch's reach. To spit at you it dives low, and for that moment the torch can hit it, if you time the swing. |
| Lodeback | 120 | Never hunts. It finds a vein with no building within 10 cells and no pilot within 8, eats 1.5 ore a second into its sac, up to 60, and walks off out of sight. Hit it and it flees. Kill it and the sac bursts: the ore goes back into the vein. |
| The Matriarch | 6,000 | 9.5 cells tall, she never leaves her nest in Slag Pockets, two regions from the start. [She's in the world now.](https://ringshadow.com/blog/matriarch) |

The numbers are tuned so you count the group before you walk in. One Shardling is no threat, two cost a fresh pilot about half its hp, and five kill it in about five seconds. A pack of six on a Hab Dome takes it down in about 40 seconds: a raid has to be answered, and there's time to get there.

## The models

The agent built a blockout model of each from the paintings, sized against the Prospector, and 49 sounds for them: idle chitter, bites, wingbeats, the swarm coming. The models are rough on purpose for now. A pass that takes them closer to the paintings (the Matriarch's crown and sac, the opal quills, the Lodeback's glass sac) is queued. [It has landed since.](https://ringshadow.com/blog/brood-art)

## The blockout models

- ![The four bug models in a row beside the Prospector, the Matriarch towering over the rest](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-brood/05-lineup.webp) The family for scale: Matriarch, Lodeback, Gloamwing, Shardling, and the Prospector.
- ![The Shardling blockout model with white quills and teal eyes](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-brood/06-shardling.webp) Shardling.
- ![The Gloamwing blockout model with violet wings and a striped glowing abdomen](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-brood/07-gloamwing.webp) Gloamwing.
- ![The Lodeback blockout model with a gold sac on its back](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-brood/08-lodeback.webp) Lodeback, its sac full.
- ![The Matriarch blockout model with a spine crown and a violet egg sac](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-brood/09-matriarch.webp) The Matriarch.

## In the world

A few hours later the bugs were in the game. They are units of the simulation like any other, on a side of their own, the Brood. A brood director on the server spawns groups out of sight, at the edge of a region or the foot of a cliff, and sends them to a point of interest picked by weight: deposits, wells, unopened blueprint sites, pads, buildings and, most of all, fresh starfall craters. They linger there for a few minutes, longer at night, and then walk off and vanish.

Walk into their site and the whole group turns on you. A bug that's attacking you gets a red outline and a life bar. Raids come straight for a building, and KSTR warns every pilot nearby before they arrive: BROOD SWARM, heading for the Hab Dome.

The start stays quiet. Prospect Landing has the fewest bugs of any region, none linger within 15 cells of the Citadel, and while a new pilot works through the six-step opening the brood holds back. The far corners have more, bigger groups, more often.

After the merge the suites stood at 467 core tests, 191 server tests and 69 network tests, all passing.

## The Brood arrives

- ![Shardlings lingering around an ore deposit while the Prospector watches](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-brood/10-linger.webp) Shardlings lingering at a deposit. Count them before you walk in.
- ![A Shardling biting the Prospector with the screen edged red](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-brood/11-attack.webp) A Shardling on the Prospector: red outline, hp falling.
- ![A violet Gloamwing diving low at the Prospector](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-brood/12-dive.webp) A Gloamwing diving to spit. This is the moment to swing.
- ![A Lodeback with a full gold sac walking away from the deposit](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-brood/13-lodeback-leaves.webp) A Lodeback leaving with a full sac, out of the torch's reach.
- ![A toast reading KSTR: BROOD SWARM, heading for the Hab Dome, as bugs close in](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-brood/14-raid.webp) KSTR: BROOD SWARM, a raid on the Hab Dome.

The torch can't hold off a raid alone, and it can't reach a Gloamwing in the air. The next work answers that: [guns for the realm](https://ringshadow.com/blog/defences).

# Missions, the Journal and three voices

> Ringshadow's Citadel now offers missions in three tiers, a Journal keeps them, and three narrators read every briefing: the mission officer, the Warden and a frightened radio dispatcher.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/blog/missions

14 October 2026 · M8 · The realm under siege

A pilot at level 10 asked the obvious question: now what? The Citadel answers it with a board of missions, and every briefing is read aloud by someone who sounds like they mean it.

![The Citadel's MISSIONS tab: three columns, easy, hard and perilous, two missions each](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/missions/01-board.webp)

*The MISSIONS board: easy close to home, hard past the borders, perilous in bug country.*

## The board

The Citadel's third tab is MISSIONS. It offers two missions in each of three tiers, and you can carry up to three at once. The tier says where you'll go: easy missions stay in your home region, hard ones send you into the next region over, perilous ones go to the far corners, where the bugs nest. The reward scales with the tier: an easy one pays about 8 minutes of your level's XP, a hard one 20, a perilous one 40, plus ore and MH.

Changed by the balance pass on 15 October: an easy mission now pays 3 minutes of your level's XP, a hard one 8, a perilous one 15, and half the ore: 75, 225 and 500. See [the balance post](https://ringshadow.com/blog/balance).

There are five kinds of mission: survey (drive to a marker and hold still while the scanner runs), haul (bring ore or MH home to the realm's buildings), hold (stand in a ring while the ringshadow band passes over), salvage (open a sealed site) and hunt (kill bugs). The hunts stayed switched off until the bugs existed; they went live with [the Brood](https://ringshadow.com/blog/the-brood) later the same day.

## The Journal

Press `L` and the Journal opens. Each mission you took has its briefing, what to do, your progress, the reward, and where it is on the map. The marker also shows on the compass and the minimap. And there's a button: PLAY THE BRIEFING.

## A mission from the board to done

- ![The MISSIONS tab with six offers](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/missions/01-board.webp) The board at the Citadel, Journal 0/3.
- ![The board after taking Mark the Ground: Signed up, it's in your Journal](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/missions/02-signed-up.webp) Signed up for Mark the Ground. It's in the Journal.
- ![The Journal: Mark the Ground with its briefing, instructions, progress, reward and a map of the regions](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/missions/03-journal.webp) The Journal (`L`): briefing, what to do, 890 XP, 200 ore, 60 MH, and where.
- ![The Prospector driving across open ground toward the mission marker](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/missions/04-marker.webp) Out to the marker. Open ground, clear sky.
- ![The banner MISSION DONE: MARK THE GROUND over the Prospector](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/missions/05-done.webp) MISSION DONE: the reward lands in the wallet.

## Three voices

Every mission template has a narration, 16 in all, read by one of three voices picked by the mission's mood. The Citadel's mission officer gives the everyday jobs and sounds like someone who enjoys them. The Warden gives the holds and the hunts, grave and fearless. The perilous missions come over the radio from KSTR's night dispatcher, on a bad line, and the dispatcher is scared.

The lines were recorded with ElevenLabs once, ahead of time, levelled to the same loudness (-18 LUFS) and shipped with the game as sound files, so the game carries no API key. The text in the Journal is what the narrator reads, word for word. Listen:

### The mission officer · Mark the Ground (easy)

[Audio](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/missions/survey-easy.m4a) "Mission officer here. Geology wants fresh readings, and you have the best seat in the realm. Drive out to the marker, sit tight, and let the scanner sing. Open ground, clear sky. Enjoy the view on the way."

### The Warden · Thin the Swarm (hard)

[Audio](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/missions/hunt-hard.m4a) "This is the Warden. The Brood is gathering beyond our borders, more of them every night. Cross over and break them before they break us. There is no glory in it. Only the work. Do it well."

### KSTR dispatch · Into the Nest (perilous)

[Audio](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/missions/hunt-perilous.m4a) "Dispatch to pilot. Oh, no. They want a cull. In the far country, where the big ones are, where the Matriarch sings. Pilot, if it goes bad, you turn around. You hear me? Nobody's ore is worth your hide out there."

The missions sit beside KSTR's daily radio contracts, which stay. The suites after this task: 458 core tests, 177 server tests, 67 network tests, all passing. The narration was checked offline, as WAV files, since agents run the game silently.


---

# The realm: shared buildings, a tax and a shop

> Ringshadow's buildings now belong to the realm: every pilot uses them, the Citadel takes 10% of every unload, and its shop sells blueprints and supplies.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/blog/the-realm

14 October 2026 · M8 · The realm under siege

I played the new mode to level 10 and came away with a list. First on it were the buildings: a world with many pilots can't give each of them a Citadel, so the buildings had to belong to everyone.

![A Prospector unloading at the Citadel, the label reading +24 ORE, 3 TO THE REALM](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-realm/01-tax.webp)

*27 ore unloaded: 24 to the pilot, 3 to the realm.*

## Buildings belong to the realm

Every building in a world is now the realm's. Any pilot unloads at any Citadel or Hab Dome, respawns at it, lands at its pads and, soon, is defended by its guns. The builder still gets the credit: the game keeps who built what, under a callsign of the form "Pilot XXXX", made from a hash of the pilot's key (the key itself never goes over the wire). A realm gets one Citadel; a later pilot's "build the Citadel" step points at the one already standing.

Old saves move over on their own: the save format went to version 8 and every old building became the realm's, with its builder kept.

## The Citadel's tax

Every unload pays the realm 10%. It rounds to the nearest whole unit, takes at least 1, and never the whole load, so a tiny unload still leaves you something. The money goes into a realm wallet, shown at the Citadel and in the HUD.

Press `H` at the Citadel and its screen opens on the REALM tab: the realm wallet, the tax, what you have paid, and buttons to donate 100, 1,000 or everything you carry. The realm wallet will pay for the Citadel's own guns, which are being built now ([coming next](https://ringshadow.com/blog/defences)).

## The realm's tax

- ![The Prospector at the Citadel with the label +24 ORE, 3 TO THE REALM](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-realm/01-tax.webp) An unload at the Citadel: +24 ORE, 3 TO THE REALM.
- ![The Citadel screen on its REALM tab: the realm wallet at 3 ore, the 10% tax, donate buttons](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-realm/02-citadel.webp) The Citadel screen (`H`): the realm wallet holds the 3 ore of tax.
- ![The REALM tab after a donation: 1,003 ore in the realm wallet](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-realm/03-donated.webp) After a donation of 1,000: "Every pilot's Citadel thanks you."

## The shop

The Citadel's second tab is a shop, paid from your own wallet. It sells every blueprint and four supplies. A blueprint is used up by one building, and copies stack, so you can buy three Hab Domes' worth before a trip. Prices rise with the blueprint's level floor and with every copy you buy: a blueprint costs (50 + 25F) × 1.5ⁿ ore and 5F × 1.5ⁿ MH, where F is its level floor and n the copies you already bought. The big ones open late: the Spacedock at level 35, the Bastion at 45, the Sentinel at 55.

| Supply | Key | What it does | Price |
|---|---|---|---|
| Repair kit | `1` | Mends half the Prospector's hp at once | 120 ore, 10 MH |
| MH canister | `2` | 25 MH into the wallet, for jets and flights | 150 ore |
| Shield charge | `3` | No damage taken for 8 s | 100 ore, 30 MH |
| Survey flare | `4` | Sites and deposits nearby show on the map for 60 s | 80 ore, 15 MH |

The shield charge exists because of what came next that same day: [the Brood](https://ringshadow.com/blog/the-brood). Sites in the world still give a free blueprint when you open one, so exploring keeps paying.

## The shop

- ![The SHOP tab: eight blueprints with stacks and prices, four supplies](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-realm/04-shop.webp) The SHOP tab: blueprints on the left, supplies on the right.
- ![The build menu listing each building with the number of blueprint copies held](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-realm/05-build-menu.webp) The build menu counts your copies: Hab Dome ×10.
- ![The Prospector in the open with a shield charge running](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/the-realm/06-shield.webp) A shield charge running: 8 seconds of no damage.

Under the hood this was three tasks by the agents (R1, C1 and C2), three network protocol versions and three save versions, each with a migration so yesterday's worlds still load. After the shop landed the suites stood at 458 core tests, 167 server tests and 67 network tests, all passing.


---

# How we got here

> Two days of building Ringshadow's MMORPG mode: our own server, a world that lasts, a hundred levels, the ringshadow sweep and starfall.

Source: https://ringshadow.com/blog/how-we-got-here

14 October 2026 · The MMORPG mode · M1 to M7

Two days ago Ringshadow's online mode was a list of decisions in a log file. Tonight a pilot lands on a frontier world, drills opal ore under a ringed giant, and watches a meteor come down where the radio said it would. Here is how it got built.

[Video: A one-minute showreel of the MMORPG mode: the home screen, a touchdown, drilling, the ringshadow band, a starfall and a dusk lift-off](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/how-we-got-here/showreel.mp4)

*The showreel: one minute, recorded from the game by an agent in a hidden run. It has the game's own sound.*

Ringshadow started as a real-time strategy game, and that game is still here. On 13 October I decided to build a second way to play next to it: you are one pilot in a world that lasts. You drive the machine yourself, you build with other pilots, and the open ground between the cities is fought over.

The first rule was that single player comes first, on a local server, and that this local server is the very program a public world will run. Only the host changes. So everything below runs through a real server, even when you play alone.

## The plumbing: M1 to M5

The agents wrote our own networking on UDP. The server is authoritative and steps the world 60 times a second; it sends each pilot only what is near them, 20 times a second, as differences. The game predicts your Prospector and corrects it, and that was tested under made-up lag, jitter and loss before anything else was built on it.

Then came a world map of three by three regions you drive across or fly between. The server saves the world to SQLite every 5 seconds; the test kills the server with kill -9 and checks that the Citadel and the Prospector are back. The traffic is encrypted (X25519 and XChaCha20-Poly1305, through the public-domain Monocypher library), and the server travels inside the Mac app.

Every screen got checked picture by picture: a shot harness drives the game in hidden runs and saves stills. The first pass took 17 pictures and found 18 problems.

## The long road: M6

On the 13th I handed the mode to a manager agent for a week, with one goal: a complete, beautiful game by 20 October. It runs workers in their own copies of the repository and merges what they finish.

M6 gave the Prospector a road worth a hundred hours.

- 100: levels
- 65: skill nodes in five branches
- 1.1 h: to level 10
- 97 h: to level 100

The XP curve is 500 + 3L² per level. Buildings come from blueprints you find in the world, each with a level floor. The server owns the world's clock: a day is 40 minutes, 30 of light and 10 of night, and the weather comes from the server too, so every pilot in a world sees the same storm.

## A world worth crossing: M7

The game is named after the giant in its sky, so the signature event had to be its shadow. Its rings throw a band of shadow that sweeps across the land on the world clock. Under it the ore veins flare and drilling pays more.

Then starfall: two or three times a world day a meteor streaks in, and its crater holds a deposit about three times richer than the usual one. First come, first served. KSTR 88.7, the frontier's only radio station, now hands out three contracts a day, and a guided opening of six steps walks a new pilot from the landing pad to the first skill point (level 4 at 1,712 XP). Flights burn Metallic Hydrogen: 10 plus 5 for every step across the map.

Work crashed twice on the 14th, once mid-morning and once mid-afternoon, and every worker was restarted from scratch. Picture runs spent about 85% of their time waiting for the game clock to reach dusk, so an agent added a clock jump for test runs: the starfall run went from 3 minutes 50 seconds to 44 seconds.

At the end of M7 the test suites stood at 454 core tests, 153 server tests and 67 network tests, all passing.

- ![The Prospector drilling an opal-flecked Stardust Ore rock, sparks flying](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/how-we-got-here/04-drilling.webp) Drilling Stardust Ore at Prospect Landing.
- ![Gold light columns rising from blueprint sites at dusk](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/how-we-got-here/05-site-columns.webp) Blueprint sites mark themselves with gold columns at dusk.
- ![The giant's rings casting a dark band across the sky and land](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/how-we-got-here/06-ringshadow.webp) The ringshadow: the rings' shadow crossing the land.
- ![A meteor's blinding impact behind the Prospector, with a KSTR STARFALL DOWN banner](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/how-we-got-here/07-starfall.webp) KSTR: STARFALL DOWN. A rich deposit in the crater.
- ![A glowing crater at night, embers floating above a molten deposit](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/how-we-got-here/08-crater.webp) The crater at night, the deposit still molten.
- ![The Prospector lifting off on jets in front of the giant at dusk](https://ringshadow.com/blog/media/how-we-got-here/09-liftoff.webp) A dusk lift-off, burning Metallic Hydrogen.

The next post is about what I asked for after playing it myself, up to level 10: [the realm](https://ringshadow.com/blog/the-realm).
